GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION  
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1208  
ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026  
 
Assessment of Quality of Education Imparted in Schools 
 
1208. Shri Janardan Singh Sigriwal: 
 
Will the Minister of Education be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has conducted any recent assessment of the quality of 
education imparted in schools and higher educational institutions in the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof including the key findings regarding learning outcomes, 
teacher quality and infrastructure in Government and private institutions, 
State/UT-wise; 
(c) whether the Government has identified any gaps in foundational literacy and 
numeracy, digital learning and teacher training affecting the quality of education; 
(d) if so, the details thereof, alongwith the corrective measures taken or proposed 
under various schemes and programmes to improve the quality of education; and 
(e) whether the Government has fixed any measurable target s and timelines for 
improving educational quality in accordance with the objectives of the National 
Education Policy 2020 and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY)  
(a) to (e): Education falls under the Concurrent List of the Constitution, with majority 
of the Schools and Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) coming under the purview of 
States and UTs. On its part, the Ministry of Education is guided by the National 
Education Policy 2020 wh ich emphasizes holistic development of learners and 
assessment practices by shifting from rote and summative examinations to regular, 
formative and competency-based assessment that promotes learning, critical thinking, 
conceptual understanding and continuous improvement in teaching-learning processes. 
 

In pursuance of the recommendations of NEP 2020, the National Assessment 
Centre, PARAKH (Performance Assessment, Review and Analysis of Knowledge for 
Holistic Development), was established by the Ministry of Education on 8th February, 
2023. PARAKH lays down norms, standards and guidelines for student assessment and 
evaluation across schools and monitors the health of the school education system 
through large -scale assessments such as the PARAKH Rashtriya Sarve kshan 
(previously National Achievement Survey), conducted from time to time. 
 
The PARAKH Rashtriya Sarvekshan (PRS) 2024 was conducted in December 
2024 to measure the baseline performance under NEP 2020 in the development of 
competencies among students at the end of Foundational, Preparatory and Middle 
Stages of Education i.e. Grades 3, 6 and 9, respectively. The survey provides district -
level evidence on learning outcomes and contextual factors to support evidence -based 
interventions for improving the quality of school education. 
 
Over 21.15 lakh students and 2.70 lakh teachers and school leaders from more 
than 74,000 schools across 781 districts in all States and Union Territories participated 
in the survey, making it one of the most extensive assessments of student learning 
conducted in the country. The findings of PARAKH Rashtriya Sarvekshan 2024 
highlight a significant improvement when compared to NAS 21 scores in foundational 
literacy and numeracy skills, thereby, reflecting the positive impact of the N IPUN 
Bharat Mission launched under NEP 2020.   
 
In order to identify possible factors affecting learning performance and enables 
evidence-based interventions to improve learning outcomes, data was also collected on 
contextual variables such as teacher trai ning, pedagogical approaches and teaching 
learning material used, home environment and resources, digital access and exposure, 
school support, school infrastructure and inclusivity, community participation etc, 
during the PARAKH Rashtriya Sarvekshan. National, State and District level reports 
for PARAKH Rashtriya Sarvekshan 2024 are accessible at 
https://dashboard.parakh.ncert.gov.in/en, a dedicated dashboard designed to 
disseminate the findings of the assessment. 
 
 
Insofar as higher education is concerned, the National Assessment and 
Accreditation Council (NAAC) assesses and accredits Higher Educational Institutions 
(HEIs) in its quality  pursuits and grades them for their achievements. Besides, the 
National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) launched in 2015 by the Government 
of India ranks HEIs based on key parameters such as “Teaching, Learning and 
Resources,” “Research and Professional Practices,” “Graduation Outcomes,” “Outreach 
and Inclusivit y,” and “Peer Perception”. The  ranking is announced every year and 
published on the NIRF website, which is available to all stakeholders as well as to the 
general public.  
 
 

The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 provides different timelines, 
principles and methodology for its implementation. Diverse interventions under various 
schemes aim to improve quality of education.  The Centrally Sponsored Scheme of 
Samagra Shiksha focuses on improvement of quality of education by providing support 
to all States and UTs for different interventions, like in-service training of teachers and 
school heads, composite school grant to every school for providing a conducive learning 
environment, support for children with special needs (CwSN), grants for library, sports 
and physical activities, support for Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan, Tinkering Labs, ICT 
and digital initiatives, school leadership development programme, remedial teaching 
for academ ically weaker students, introduction of new pedagogical and curricular 
structure, NIPUN Bharat Initiative, child friendly and inclusive classrooms including 
ECCE facilities, strengthening of School Management Committees (SMCs) and 
community led initiatives , opening, strengthening/upgradation of residential 
schools/hostels, free uniforms to eligible children and free text books at elementary 
level, transport allowance and undertaking enrolment & retention drives , provision of 
transport allowance and undertak ing enrolment & retention drives. Further, under the 
Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (PM POSHAN), 
one hot cooked meal is provided to the students at elementary level (including 
Balvatika) in Government and Government -aided schools to take -care of their 
nutritional requirements and improve attendance. As part of the Centrally Sponsored 
Scheme of Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India (PM SHRI) , existing schools are 
being strengthened to showcase all aspects of NEP 2020 and function as exemplar 
schools. The objective is to enhance quality of education through emphasis on 
foundational literacy & numeracy, upgradation of infrastructure, inculcation of 
sensitivity to environmental concerns as well as enhancement of critical thin king and 
other 21st century skills through holistic, experiential and competency – based learning 
rather than rote learning.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1211 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
Sariska Tiger Reserve and Nahargarh Sanctuary 
 
1211. SHRI HANUMAN BENIWAL: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that the Ministry had sent a letter to the State Government of 
Rajasthan on May 07, 2025, for necessary action regarding the issue of illegal activities occurring 
around the Sariska Tiger Reserve and Nahargarh Sanctuary in Rajasthan; 
(b) if so, the details of action taken report received so far from the State Government of Rajasthan 
with reference to the said letter; 
(c) whether the Government has taken any action based on the report of the State Government to stop 
these illegal activities and also against the culprits and if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to conduct an independent inquiry or send a joint inspection 
team keeping in view the seriousness of the matter and if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE 
CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) A letter was sent to the State Government of Rajasthan vide F. No. WL-17/91/2025 WL dated 
23.04.2025 (and not on May 07, 2025), for taking appropriate action regarding the said issue, which 
mainly pertains to rationalisation of boundary of Sariska Tiger Reserve and demarcation of Nahargarh 
Sanctuary as per notification. 
 
(b), (c) & (d) As informed by the State, the process of rationalisation of boundary of Sariska Tiger 
Reserve was initiated as per recommendations of the Central Empowered Committee of the Hon’ble 
Supreme Court as per directions in the suo-moto case No. 1/2023, W.P. (Civil) No. 202/1995, T.N. 
Godavarman vs. Union of India. The State Government constituted a 12-Member Committee which 
has submitted its report on rationalisation of Critical Tiger Habitat and buffer of Sariska Tiger 
Reserve.  The same has been recommended by the State Board for Wildlife, National Tiger 
Conservation Authority and National Board for Wildlife.  As per directions of the Court, the draft 
notification in this regard has been issued by the State Government and public hearing by District 
Collectors of Alwar and Kotputli-Bahrod has been completed.  The matter is sub-judice in the 
Hon’ble Supreme Court. 
 
In so far as Nahargarh Sanctuary is concerned, Hon’ble NGT, Bhopal constituted a team in OA 
97/2022 on 16.12.2024 to demarcate and revise the map of the said Sanctuary in accordance with the 
notification.  The same has been challenged in the Hon’ble High Court in W.P. (Civil) No. 
14254/2025.  The matter is sub-judice.

UNORGANISED SECTOR 
 
†1212. SMT. ANITA NAGARSINGH CHOUHAN: 
 
         Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)whether a large number of workers in the tribal and rural areas of 
Ratlam Lok Sabha Constituency of Madhya Pradesh are engaged in 
the unorganized sector and many of them are  still deprived of the 
benefits available under social security, e -Shram registration, 
health security and labour codes; 
(b)if so, the details of workers registered on the e -Shram portal, 
workers benefitted under  social security schemes and 
establishments registered und er the new labour codes in Ratlam,  
Jhabua and Alirajpur districts of the said Constituency; 
(c)whether any special campaign or action plan is operational in the 
said area for effective implementation of labour codes, registration 
of workers, health securit y, skill development and to  enhance 
awareness; and 
(d)if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (d): The Ministry of Labour and Employment launched eShram 
portal (eshram.gov.in) on 26th August 2021 for creation of a 
comprehensive National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW) 
seeded with Aadhaar. eShram portal is meant to register and support 
the unorgan ised workers by providing them a Universal Account 
Number (UAN) on a self-declaration basis. 
 
  Over 31.80 crore unorganised workers have already been 
registered on eShram portal. 
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
  In the State of Madhya Pradesh, the total number of 
registrations recorded are 2,44,280 in Ratlam district, 1,26,664 in 
Jhabua district, and 81,766 in Alirajpur district. 
 
  District-wise details of unorganised workers registered 
under various schemes on t he eShram portal in State of Madhya 
Pradesh is annexed. 
 
  The number of establishments registered under the new 
Labour Codes in Ratlam, Jhabua and Alirajpur districts are 26, 06 and 
04 respectively as on 23.07.2026. 
 
  The Government of India has implemen ted four Labour 
Codes, namely, the Code on Wages, 2019, the Industrial Relations 
Code, 2020, the Code on Social Security, 2020 and the Occupational 
Safety, Health and Working Conditions (OSH&WC) Code, 2020 with 
effect from 21 st November, 2025. The Central Rules under the said 
Codes have been notified on 08.05.2026.  ‘Labour’ being in the 
concurrent list, the States/UTs are also required to frame Rules under 
the Labour Codes for uniform implementation of the Codes. 
  
  The four Labour Codes envisage strengthe ning the 
protection available to all workers, including unorganized workers in 
terms of statutory minimum wage and its timely payment, social 
security, occupational safety, healthcare of workers etc. 
Simultaneously, it also strengthens the protection avail able to 
workers, including unorganized workers and promote formalization of 
workforce. 
  
  The four Labour Codes are applicable to whole of the 
country including tribal and rural areas. All the benefits under the said 
Labour Codes are also applicable to all workers, including organized 
and unorganized workers in these areas.

wise, with particular reference to Krishna district, since its implementation; 
(b) whether it is a fact that the Government is proposing to ease rules to companies 
and also students to allow Post Graduates, MBAs, etc., in PMIS, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(c) whether Phase-III has been launched, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the number of participating companies in Phase-I, II and III; 
(e) the efforts being made by the Government to increase participation and reduce 
high dropout rate under this scheme; and 
(f) whether there is any proposal to increase the monthly stipend from the present 
Rs. 6000 per month and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS AND MINISTRY OF 
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS                                                                                           
 [SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA] 
(a): District wise details of  offers made by the companies, offers accepted  by 
candidates and candidates joined from the state of Andhra Pradesh, including 
Krishna district, in Round I, Round II and Round III of the PMIS Pilot Project is placed 
at Annexure I. Round III of the PMIS Pilot project is ongoing. 
(b): The revised Guidelines of the Prime Minister Internship Scheme (PMIS) – Pilot 
Project, issued vide Office Memorandum (O.M.) dated 12.03.2026, has expanded the 
categories of companies/organizations eligible to participate in the Pilot Project . 
Accordingly, top 2000 companies based on the average CSR expenditure during  the 
last three financial years, companies having a nnual turnover of more than Rs. 1,000 
crores or having net worth of more than Rs. 500 crores  during the immediatel y 
preceding financial year, and companies from under-represented sectors are eligible 

to participate  under PMIS Pilot Project.  Additionally, other organizations such as 
Professional Associations/ institutions, selected MSMEs, Global Capability Centers 
(GCCs), companies under Special Economic Zones (SEZs), statutory Authorities, 
State Government nominated companies  etc. are also eligibl e to participate  under 
the PMIS Pilot Project. 
Further, the revised Guidelines  has expanded the eligibility criteria to include 
postgraduates students to participate in PMIS Pilot Project, however, candidates 
having qualifications such as MBA or equivalent, are not eligible to participate in the 
PMIS Pilot Project.  
(c): Round III of the PMIS Pilot Project was launched on 20.03.2026 with revised 
Guidelines.  
(d):  No. of companies/organizations who have participated in the Round I, II and III 
in the PMIS Pilot Project is placed as Annexure II. 
(e): Based on the learning during the implementation of the Round I and Round II of 
the PMIS Pilot Project, following measures have been taken to increase participation 
and reduce high dropout rate under the PMIS Pilot Project: 
i. As per the revised guidelines of the PMIS Pilot Project issued vide O.M. dated 
12.03.2026 following key changes have been made:  
a. A flexible duration of internships of either 6 or 9 months based on the 
company’s requirements is provided. 
b. The monthly allowance has been enhanced from Rs. 5000 to Rs. 9000.  
c. The age requirement for youth has been relaxed from 21 –24 to 18 –25 
years. Further, candidates who have a master’s degree and students 
from final year of graduation/post-graduation are eligible. 
d. Scope of companies/organisations eligible to participate has been 
expanded.  
e. Adopted a rolling internship cycle allowing continuous posting, 
selection, and onboarding. 
ii. Portal Improvement: functionality for geo-tagging internship location, moving 
vacancies and candidates between one location to another and, more visibility of 
additional benefits given by companies to the candidates. 
iii. Targeted Information, Education and Communications (IEC) activities. 
iv. Active engagement and coordination with States, UTs, Ministries and 
Departments of the Central Government and Industry Associations for enhancing the 
outreach of the scheme. 
(f): As per the revised Guidelines issued vide O.M. dated 12.03.2026, the monthly 
assistance payable to interns has already been enhanced from ₹5,000 to ₹9,000 with 
effect from March 2026.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.1214 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
Manuscript Clusters and Partner Institutions under Gyan Bharatam   Initiative 
 
1214. Shri B K Parthasarathi: 
 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the details of the number and list of manuscript clusters and partner institutions 
identified under the Gyan Bharatam Initiative, along with the criteria adopted for their 
selection, State/UT-wise; 
 
(b) the details of the number of manuscripts identified, digitised, conserved and restored 
under the Initiative, including manuscripts catalogued and made publicly accessible, 
State/UT-wise; 
 
(c) the details of the funds sanctioned, released and utilised under the said Initiative, 
State/UT and year-wise, since its inception; 
 
(d) the details of the measures taken to preserve, digitise and promote Telugu-language 
manuscripts, including details of partner institutions, projects supported and manuscripts 
covered in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana; and 
 
(e) whether the Government proposes to expand the network of manuscript clusters and 
digitisation facilities, particularly for regional language manuscripts and if so, the details 
thereof along with timeline for implementation? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM 
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) The Gyan Bharatam Mission (GBM) has been mandated to establish a nation-wide 
network of Cluster Centers (CCs) and Independent Centers (ICs) across the country. These 
institutions have been selected based on prescribed criteria, including the size and 
significance of manuscript collections, institutional capacity, availability of qualified 
manpower and infrastructure, regional representation, and experience in manuscript-related 
activities. A list of CCs/ICs onboarded so far is at annexure. 
(b)  National Manuscript Survey was launched in March, 2026 across all States and Union 
Territories of the country to identify and document manuscript holdings, repositories and 
custodians representing diverse languages and scripts. During the survey, more than 1.19 
crore manuscripts have been reported. The total number of digitized manuscripts available 
across the country is over 8 lakh, out of which, more than 3.90 lakh manuscripts are available 
on Gyan Bharatam portal at present for public access in view mode. 
 
 
 

 
(c)  The year-wise budget sanctioned and allocated under GBM is as hereunder: 
Financial Y ear Sanctioned Budget  
(In Cr.) 
Actual Expenditure  
(In Cr.)  
2024-25 3.50 2.63 
2025-26 15.00 14.25 
2026-27 60.00 4.48 
 
(d) Gyan Bharatam, is a Pan-India initiative covering cataloguing, conservation, digitization 
and publication of manuscripts identified across the country. For effective implementation, a 
framework of Cluster Centres and Independent Centres has been envisaged. These centres are 
provided financial assistance in form of grant-in-aid to undertake manuscript related activities 
as elaborated above. The list of onboarded centers in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana is at 
annexure. 
(e) Gyan Bharatam envisages the identification, documentation, conservation, digitisation, 
research, publication and dissemination of India's manuscript heritage irrespective of script, 
language, dialect, tradition, community or geographical location. Eligible repositories having 
manuscripts are considered for onboarding with GBM in accordance with the Mission 
guidelines, subject to physical verification, institutional readiness and availability of 
resources, funds etc.

MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1215 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY , JULY 27, 2026/SHARAVANA 5, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
LACK OF FINANCIAL LITERACY IN RURAL AREAS 
 
1215. Shri Babu Singh Kushwaha: 
        Shri Neeraj Maurya: 
        Shri Lalji Verma: 
        Shri Devesh Shakya: 
        Shri Harendra Singh Malik:  
  
 Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that despite investor awareness programmes, 
financial literacy continues to be lacking in rural areas in the country, especially in 
Etah, Kasganj and Jaunpur Lok Sabha Constituencies in Uttar Pradesh, where the 
people are still losing money to Ponzi schemes and financial frauds, if so, the details 
thereof along with the steps taken by the Government to improve the situation; 
(b) whether any independent audit has been conducted regarding the funds being 
utilized by the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF) Authority and the actual 
benefits (outcomes) received by the investors in comparison to it, if so, the details 
thereof; 
 (c) whether a provision for penal action is likely to be made against companies that 
deliberately delay the claims and harass investors by raising unnecessary technical 
shortcomings such as signature mismatch or other minor flaws in their claims, if so, 
the details thereof; and 
 (d) whether the Government proposes to bring any special relief scheme to simplify 
the cumbersome process of filing claims and obtaining a succession certificate for 
the legal heirs of deceased investors and if so, the details thereof?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS AND MINISTRY OF 
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(HARSH MALHOTRA) 
 
(a): Improving f inancial literacy is a continuous effort. I nvestor awareness 
programmes are organized  by Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority 
(IEPFA) in collaboration with professional bodies, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) 
and other stakeholders to create awareness regarding safe investing, prevention of 
financial frauds, Ponzi schemes and unregulated deposit schemes. 
 

These programmes are conducted across States and Union Territories, inclu ding the 
Etah, Kasganj and Jaunpur Lok Sabha Districts . Awareness material is also 
disseminated through digital platforms, social media, print media and electronic 
media.     
(b): Impact Assessment on the outcomes achieved  is prepared as part of the 
monitoring and evaluation process for investor awareness programmes conducted in 
collaboration with India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) and by the Financial Markets and 
Investors' Awareness Committee of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India 
(ICAI) through its Programme Organising Units (PoUs) .  Almost 98% participants 
attended the Camps found them useful and relevant for the financial needs.  
(c): The provisions relating to submission and verification of claims are governed 
by the Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority (Accounting, Audit, Transfer 
and Refund) Rules, 2016. As per Rule 7(3) of IEPF (AATR) Rules,2016,  inter alia, 
provides the following 
“ Provided also that for failure to submit verification report of the claim in accordance 
with these rules, the  company and its Nodal Officer shall be punishable as per the 
provisions of the Act’ 
(d): IEPFA vide  notification dated 9 th September, 2024 has simplified the  claim 
process for transferring securities to legal heirs through legal heir certificates issued 
by revenue authorities. The requirement for furnishing a succession certificate is not 
mandatory in cases involving transmission of securities where the value of the claim 
does not exceed ₹5 lakh per issuer company in case of securities held in physical 
mode and ₹ 15 lakhs for s ecurities held in dematerialised mode, subject to the 
claimant submitting the other prescribed documents in accordance with the 
provisions of the Rules.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.1217 
ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
DEVELOPMENT OF CULTURAL INFRASTRUCTURE IN GHAZIABAD 
 
 
1217.   SHRI ATUL GARG: 
 
Will the MINISTER OF CULTURE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has provided systematic financial grants to establish and upgrade 
cultural infrastructure, including auditoriums and public libraries, in Ghaziabad Lok Sabha 
Constituency; 
(b) if so, the details of the total central funds disbursed to support local cultural organizations 
and regional literary research within the said Constituency during 2025-26; 
(c) whether the Government is funding the establishment of a dedicated regional museum in 
Ghaziabad to safely house local historical artifacts and traditional handicrafts; 
(d) the details of the support provided to local youth clubs working to preserve traditional art 
forms and classical music in the National Capital Region; and  
(e) the details of the future initiatives planned to integrate local cultural education into the 
regional school curriculum to foster deep historical awareness among the youth of 
Ghaziabad? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM 
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) & (b) : The Ministry of Culture administers the following two schemes under which financial 
support is provided to NGO, Trust, Societies, Govt. Sponsored bodies, State / UT Govt. 
University, Central/State Govt. agencies/bodies, Municipal Corporations, reputed not-for-profit 
organizations etc. for creation of Cultural Spaces such as Auditorium with facilities and 
infrastructure for stage performances (dance, drama and music), exhibitions, seminars, literary 
activities, green rooms, etc.  The Scheme component also provides support for restoration, 
renovation, extension, alteration, up-gradation, modernization of existing cultural facilities 
(Rabindra Bhawans, Rangshalas) etc.: - 
 
(i) Financial Assistance for Construction of Tagore Cultural Complexes (TCC); & 
(ii) Financial Assistance for Building Grants including Studio Theatres. 
 
The Scheme brief of above schemes is given at Annexure-I. 
 

Further, Library being a state subject, establishment and functioning of public libraries 
comes under the purview of the respective State Government/UT Authorities. However, Raja 
Rammohun Roy Library Foundation (RRRLF), Kolkata, has been providing financial assistance 
for the development of public libraries across the country including Uttar Pradesh under its 
various approved Matching and Non-matching schemes which encompasses the purpose to 
enrich the knowledge resources of public library, procurement of library furniture, construction 
of library building, for establishment of children corner, knowledge corner and for creation of 
facilities for Divyangjan Readers and modernization of public library services by procuring 
computers, printers etc. with active cooperation of the respective State / UT Library Authority. 
Financial assistance under various schemes of RRRLF is released based on the eligible 
recommended application submitted by the State/UTs public library authority duly approved by 
the State Level Planning Committee (SLPC). Financial assistance released through RRRLF 
schemes for development of public libraries in Uttar Pradesh including Ghaziabad during 2025-
26 based on the eligible and recommended application submitted by the Uttar Pradesh State 
library authority is provided at Annexure-II. 
Under the National Mission on Libraries (NML) Scheme, financial assistance is provided 
under the "Setting up of NML Model Libraries" component to one State Central Library and one 
District Library in each State/UT. The details of financial assistance provided under the NML 
Scheme in the State of Uttar Pradesh are also given at Annexure-III. 
(c):  No. 
(d) : The Ministry of Culture implements a Central Sector Scheme ‘Kala Sanskriti Vikas Yojana 
(KSVY) under which financial assistance is provided through various scheme components for 
the promotion, preservation and dissemination of India's traditional art forms, classical music 
and cultural heritage. Under these schemes, eligible cultural organizations, institutions and 
registered societies, including those engaged in training and promotion of traditional arts and 
classical music, may avail financial assistance subject to fulfilment of the prescribed guidelines 
and eligibility criteria. 
In the National Capital Region (NCR), youth clubs are not provided financial assistance 
under any separate scheme exclusively meant for them. However, eligible organizations working 
with youth for the preservation and promotion of traditional art forms, classical music and other 
cultural activities may receive support under the Ministry's existing scheme-based framework, 
such as the Scheme for Financial Assistance for Promotion of Art and Culture and other relevant 
schemes, based on merit, availability of funds and adherence to the scheme guidelines. 
(e): There is no such proposal under consideration of the Ministry.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TOURISM 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.1218  
ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
INFRASTRUCTURE STATUS FOR HOSPITALITY SECTOR 
 
1218. SHRI ESWARASAMY K: 
 SHRI ANURAG SHARMA: 
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has considered granting full Infrastructure 
Status to the hospitality and hotel sector to promote tourism, attract 
investment and generate employment, beyond projects limited to 
select destinations across the country and if so, the d etails and 
present status thereof along with the timelines for its implementation 
and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(b) whether granting such a status is expected to help in enhancing 
Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), improving access to long -term 
institutional finance at competitive rates to address the current 
accommodation and hospitality infrastructure constraints and 
strengthening tourism infrastructure, particularly in Tier-II and Tier-III 
cities and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the details of the “Challenge Mode” initiative announced in Budget 
2025-26 to develop 50 top tourist destinations, including the criteria 
for selection, financial outlays and implementation framework and the 
destinations selected from Uttar Pradesh; 
(d) whether the Government proposes to extend similar support to 
emerging tourism destinations, particularly the Bundelkhand region, 
including Jhansi, considering its historical, cultural and heritage 
significance; and  
(e) the details of the steps taken/being taken to promote sustainable 
tourism, heritage conservation and private sector participation in such 
regions? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM           (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a): Yes. The Government granted infrastructure status under the 
Harmonized Master List to the following hospitality and hotel sector: 

(i) three-star or higher category classified hotels located outside cities 
with population of more than 1 million are granted infrastructure 
status by the Government of India. 
(ii) Ropeways and cable cars 
(iii) Exhibition-cum-Convention Centre (with minimum built-up floor area* 
of 100,000 square metres of exclusively exhibition space or 
convention space or both combined). 
 
(b): The grant of infrastructure status enables eligible projects to access 
infrastructure financing, subject to applicable regulatory and lending 
norms, thereby facilitating the availability of long-term, patient capital for 
investment in tourism infrastructure facilitating investments in the sector 
including Foreign Direct Investments. 
 
(c) to (e): The Budget Speech for the year 2025 –26 announced that Top 
50 tourist destination sites in the country will be developed in partnership 
with states (including Uttar Pradesh) through a challenge mode. Land for 
building key infrastructure will have to be prov ided by states resulting in 
inclusion of hotels in those destinations in the infrastructure Harmonized 
Master List. 
 
Development of tourism infrastructure at different destinations and 
assessing environmental and social impact is primarily done by the 
concerned State Government/UT Administration. However, Ministry of 
Tourism under its various schemes including ‘Swadesh D arshan (SD)’, 
‘Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0)’ and ‘Challenge Based Destination 
Development – CBDD’ (an initiative under Swadesh Darshan scheme) 
provides financial assistance for development of tourism infrastructure 
and experiences in the country including i n rural and border areas, on 
receipt of the project proposals from State Governments/UT 
Administrations, in synergy with the scheme guidelines, Government 
directions, availability of funds, inter -se priority etc. Similarly, financial 
assistance to undertake projects is also provided to State Government/UT 
Administration under ‘Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Heritage 
Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD)’ scheme with the idea to integrate 
development of identified pilgrimage and heritage destinations. 
 
Various aspects of sustainability including environmental 
sustainability, socio-cultural sustainability and economic sustainability are 
embedded in the scheme ideation.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1219 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
SOCIAL SECURITY AND WELFARE OF EMPLOYEES IN THE PRIVATE 
SECTOR 
†1219. SMT. SANDHYA RAY: 
 
         Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)whether a large number of youth are deprived of facilities like 
social security, pension and  insurance despite working in the 
private sector; 
(b)whether the Government proposes to develop an integrated social 
security system for the  unorganised and contractual employees 
working in the private sector; 
(c)if so, the details thereof; 
(d)whether any timeline has been fixed in this regard; and 
(e)if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (e): To ensure social security coverage of organized sector 
workers, the following schemes are being implemented by Employees 
Provident Fund Organization (EPFO).  
(i) The Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 2026 (EPF);  
(ii) The Employees’ Pension Scheme, 2026 (EPS); 
(iii) The Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme, 2026 (EDLI). 
          These schemes are aimed at providing comprehensive 
social security to organized sector workers by ensuring retirement 
savings, monthly pension on superannuation/disability, and insurance 
benefits to dependents in case of death during service. 
        This Ministry has launched Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi 
Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) scheme in February 2019 in order to provide old 
age protection to the workers of unorganized sector. This is a 
voluntary and contributory pension scheme. Under the scheme, a 
monthly assured pension of Rs. 3000/- is provided to the unorganized  
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
workers after attaining the age of 60 years. The workers in the age 
group of 18 to 40 years whose monthly income is Rs. 15,000/- or less 
and not a member of EPFO/ESIC/NPS (Govt. funded) are eligible to join 
the scheme. 
  The Union Cabinet, on 1 July 2025, approved the 
Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) Scheme, titled the Pradhan Mantri 
Viksit Bharat Rojg ar Yojana (PMVBRY), to promote employment 
generation, enhance employability, and strengthen social security 
across all sectors, with a particular focus on the manufacturing 
sector. The scheme was launched on 15th August 2025. The scheme 
has a registration period of two years from 01.08.2025 to 31.07.2027 
and a budgetary outlay of ₹99,446 Crore. The scheme aims to 
incentivise creation of more than 3.5 Crore jobs all across the 
country. 
       For the first time, the definition of ‘gig workers’ and 
‘platform workers’ and provisions related to the same have been 
made in the Code on Social Security, 2020 which has come into force 
w.e.f. 21.11.2025. 
        The Code provides for framing of suitable social security 
measures for gig workers and platform workers on matters relating 
to life and disability cover, accident insurance, health and maternity 
benefits, old age protection, etc. The Code provides for setting up a 
Social Security Fund to finance welfare schemes. The Code also has 
provisions to constitute a Nati onal Social Security Board for the 
purposes of the welfare of gig workers and platform workers. 
        Various schemes of different Central 
Ministries/Departments have already been integrated/ mapped with 
the e -Shram to enhance social security coverage to  unorganized 
workers, such as Pradhan Mantri Street Vendors Atmanirbhar Nidhi 
(PMSVANidhi),Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY), 
Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), Mahatma 
Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee scheme (MGNREGS), 
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G), Ayushman Bharat – 
Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY), Pradhan Mantri Awas 
Yojana – Urban (PMAY-U), Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana 
(PMMSY), Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM -KISAN), One 
Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) and Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana 
Yojana (PMMVY), etc.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TOURISM 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.1220 
ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
SUSTAINABLE TOURISM AND  
CARRYING CAPACITY OF TOURIST DESTINATIONS 
 
1220. SHRI RAMASAHAYAM RAGHURAM REDDY:   
SHRI MANISH TEWARI:    
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the impact of the rapid growth 
in domestic tourism on the carrying capacity of major tourist 
destinations, particularly hill stations, coastal regions, pilgrimage 
centres and eco-sensitive areas;  
(b) whether the Government has identified tourist destinations facing 
overcrowding, traffic congestion, waste generation, water scarcity, 
pollution and pressure on civic infrastructure and if so, the details 
thereof, State/UT-wise;  
(c) whether the Government has issued any sustainability guidelines for 
hotels, tourism operators and Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and 
Exhibitions (MICE) tourism activities and if so, the details thereof;  
(d) whether the Government proposes to formulate a national framework 
for sustainable tourism, including destination carrying capacity 
assessments, visitor management plans and promotion of lesser -
known destinations;  
(e) the details of financial assistance provided for tourism infrastructure 
and civic amenities in high -footfall destinations, States/UT -wise 
during the last five years; and  
(f) the details of the steps taken to promote responsible tourism, 
improve coordination with States and local bodies, and ensure 
environmentally sustainable tourism development? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM            (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) & (b): The development, promotion, and assessment of tourist 
destinations including evaluating the environmental and socio -cultural 

 
impacts of over -tourism, infrastructure stress, carrying capacity, waste 
accumulation, and water shortages -are primarily undertaken by the 
respective State Governments and Union Territory (UT) Administrations. 
 
The Ministry of Tourism actively encourages States/UTs to undertake 
carrying capacity assessments when submitting project proposals. To 
assist with this, the Ministry has circulated a Template for Destination 
Master Plan to State Governments, which include s specific guidance on 
assessing and managing the physical carrying capacity of destinations 
based on visitor numbers and natural limiting factors like heavy rainfall or 
snowfall. 
 
(c): The Ministry of Tourism under its voluntary scheme of classification, 
classifies hotels into 1 -STAR to 5 -STAR. The Guidelines for this 
classification mandates Eco -friendly Practices viz. (i) Sewage Treatment 
Plant (ii) rain water harvesting (iii) waste management (iv) pollution control 
method for air, water and light (v) Introduction of non -CFC equipment for 
refrigeration and air conditioning and other Eco -friendly measures and 
initiatives. 
 
To position India as a leading global MICE destination, the Ministry of 
Tourism has developed a National Strategy and  Roadmap for the MICE 
industry which was circulated to all States/ UTs. 
 
The Ministry has also formulated Model Guidelines in 2024 for setting 
up City MICE Promotion Bureau (CMPB) as a single point of contact for 
facilitating MICE events and circulated to States / UTs for reference and 
adoption with suitable modifications. States have been requested to 
strengthen th e MICE ecosystem and related services and to collaborate 
with the stakeholders to attract more domestic and international meetings. 
A digital MICE catalogue highlighting MICE facilities at major destinations 
has also been prepared in 2025 by the Ministry. 
 
(d): The Ministry has formulated National Strategy for Sustainable Tourism 
and circulated to all States/UTs for necessary action.  In line with the 
strategy, Travel for LiFE programme has been initiated to 
promote sustainable tourism in the country and to encour age tourists and 
tourism businesses to adopt sustainable tourism practices.  
 
The Ministry actively promotes lesser-known destinations through the 
"Dekho Apna Desh" initiative. This involves creating awareness about 
unexplored sites via webinars, social media promotions, digital booklets, 
and regional marketing campaigns. 

 
 
(e): The primary responsibility for developing tourism destinations and 
products rests with State Governments and Union Territory 
Administrations. The Ministry of Tourism complements these regional 
efforts by providing vital financial assistance through flagship schemes like 
Swadesh Darshan (focusing destination -centric and lesser -known spots), 
Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Heritage Augmentation Drive 
(PRASHAD) and Challenge Based Destination Development (CBDD). These 
combined efforts aim to enrich the o verall visitor experience by upgrading 
core tourism infrastructure, safety, sanitation, connectivity, and wayside 
amenities. 
 
The details of projects sanctioned in the country under Swadesh 
Darshan, Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0), CBDD, PRASHAD and SASCI 
schemes is in Annexure. 
 
(f): The Government has taken several measures to promote responsible 
and sustainable tourism. A National Board for Sustainable Tourism, under 
the Chairpersonship of the Secretary (Tourism), has been constituted to 
ensure coordinated implementation of sustainab le tourism initiatives with 
the participation of Central Ministries, States/UTs and industry 
stakeholders. The Travel for LiFE (TFL) Programme, launched under Mission 
LiFE, promotes environmentally responsible behaviour among tourists and 
tourism businesses. 
 
Further, Swadesh Darshan 2.0 adopts a destination -centric approach 
for integrated, sustainable and responsible development of tourist 
destinations in partnership with States/UTs and local bodies. The Ministry 
of Tourism, in collaboration with the Ministry of Environment, Forest and 
Climate Change, has also conducted capacity -building programmes under 
the Alternate Livelihood Programme (ALP) and Paryavaran Naavik 
Certification (PNC) at selected Ramsar sites to promote nature -based 
tourism while conserving local ecosystems.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1221 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
Mist Spraying Systems for Dust Control 
 
1221. SHRI MADDILA GURUMOORTHY: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has examined the feasibility of making dust suppression systems, 
including slab-level mist spraying, mandatory for high-rise construction projects to reduce 
particulate pollution and protect public health; 
(b) whether the Government proposes to issue uniform national guidelines for mandatory 
installation and operation of mist spraying systems at major construction sites; 
(c) whether the Government has considered implementing pilot projects for such dust control 
systems in Government-funded infrastructure and building projects; 
(d) whether any standards have been prescribed or proposed to be prescribed for monitoring 
compliance with dust control measures during construction activities; and 
(e) the steps being taken to reduce construction-related air pollution and ensure effective 
implementation of dust suppression measures across the country? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE 
CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (e): CPCB has issued ‘Guidelines on dust mitigation measures in handling construction 
material and C&D wastes’ in November, 2017 and these guidelines prescribe the dust mitigation 
measures during construction activities.  
 
CPCB issued directions on 20.12.2017 to all State Pollution Control Board/Pollution Control 
Committee (SPCBs/PCCs) to make the above mentioned guidelines to be part of the Consent 
management and direct Urban Local Bodies (ULB) to ensure compliance of these guidelines at 
construction sites in their jurisdiction.  
 
CPCB issued directions on September 21, 2022 to all SPCBs/PCCs to ensure that construction and 
demolition activities are equipped with adequate dust mitigation measures, to ensure that large 
C&D activities having area more than 20,000 square meter are equipped with adequate dust 
mitigation measures including installation of anti-smog guns and also to ensure that a robust 
system of surveillance for compliance of above directions is put in place and any violation is dealt 
strictly as per law. 
 
Building and Construction projects having ≥20,000 sq. m and <1,50,000 sq. m of built-up area, 
Townships and Area Development projects covering an area ≥50 ha and /or built-up area ≥1,50,000 

sq. m. are required to obtain prior Environmental Clearance under the Environmental Impact 
Assessment Notification issued by MoEF&CC vide S.O. 1533(E) dated 14.09.2006.  
 
Such building and construction projects are required to prepare Environmental Management Plan 
and Conceptual plan and Townships and Area Development projects are required to carry out 
Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) study to assess the environmental impacts and prepare 
Environment Management Plan containing mitigation measures including air pollution mitigation 
during construction and operation phase of the project. 
 
Ministry has delegated the powers under EIA Notification, 2006 to the State Level Expert 
Appraisal Committees (SEACs) for appraisal and the State Level Environment Impact Assessment 
Authorities (SEIAAs) for grant of Environmental Clearance for building and construction projects, 
and Townships and Area Development projects. 
 
Further, State Pollution Control Board (SPCB)/Pollution Control Committees (PCC) grant 
Consent to Establish (CTE) and Consent to Operate (CTO) for Building construction projects 
under The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 and The Water (Prevention and 
Control of Pollution) Act, 1974.  
 
Building Construction Projects with built up area ≥ 20,000 sq. m. have been categorised into 
Orange (Pollution Index 55 to less than 80) and with built up area ≥ 5,000 sq. m., but < 20,000 sq. 
m. have been categorised as Green (Pollution Index 25 to less than 55) categories, based on the 
pollution potential and are monitored by the respective State Pollution Control Board/Pollution 
Control Committees during its construction and operation phases. 
 
Further, towards effective management and control of dust from the C&D activities, Ministry of 
Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) had notified the Environment (Construction 
and Demolition) Waste Management Rules, 2025, notified on 02.04.2025 vide G.S.R. 219(E). 
These rules emphasize the roles and accountability of waste generators at source and various 
stakeholders focusing on segregation, recovery, reuse, and recycling.  
 
In the revised rules, waste generators of Construction and Demolition activities have been 
mandated for recycling of C&D waste generation under Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR). 
Further, waste generators have been mandated to utilise recycled or processed waste in all 
construction activities, having built-up area of 20,000 square meters or above, and road 
construction as per the defined targets.  
 
Producers or occupiers, in-charge of construction projects have also been mandated to take steps 
to prevent air pollution, littering of waste including public nuisance during collection, segregation 
and storage of waste. The enforcement of the provisions, under the aforesaid rules, is to be carried 
out by State Pollution Control Board, Local authorities and Development Authorities.  
 
CPCB vide letter dated 25.05.2026 issued directions under section 5 of the Environment 
(Protection) Act, 1986 to all SPCB/PCCs for implementation of the Environment (Construction 
and Demolition) Management Rules, 2025, inter-alia include ensuring coordination with 
concerned State Departments for enforcement of the rules, for publication of schedule of Rates for 
recycled/processed C&D waste products for their utilization in construction and road works, 
States/UTs formulate and enforce mandatory policies for utilization of processed C&D waste in 

road construction and infrastructure projects by linking with tender documents, establishment of 
adequate C&D waste collection centres in proximity to waste generation points.  
 
Indian Road Congress (IRC) issued ‘IRC 121:2017- Guidelines for Use of Construction and 
Demolition Waste in Road Sector’. These guidelines deal with the use of processed C&D waste 
such as Recycled Aggregate (RA) and Recycled Concrete Aggregate (RCA) for road works viz. 
embankments, sub-base and base course, for manufacturing kerb stones, paving blocks and for 
replacing certain portion of aggregates used in different types of cement concrete pavements. 
 
The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) vide 
Direction Nos. 11-15 dated 11.06.2021 directed the Government of NCT of Delhi and NCR State 
Governments to put in place an online web portal for monitoring of compliance of dust mitigation 
measures by the large projects (with plot area above 500 square metres) and to ensure remote 
monitoring through technological intervention such as video fencing and ensure self-audit and 
certification mechanism by all the registered projects, in addition to other dust mitigation 
measures. Accordingly, Web portal is functional in all Delhi-NCR States. To effectively combat 
dust emissions CAQM vide Direction No. 69 dated 02.11.2022, also mandated deployment of 
adequate number of Anti-Smog Guns, in proportion to the area of the construction.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1222 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
Illegal Tree Felling and Enforcement Mechanism 
 
1222. SHRI CHAVAN RAVINDRA VASANTRAO: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has conducted any assessment regarding increase in incidents of 
illegal tree felling in urban areas, forest areas and peri-urban regions during each of last five 
years; 
(b) if so, the details of such incidents, cases registered, prosecutions launched, convictions 
secured and estimated loss of tree cover during said period; 
(c) whether the Government has identified the major causes responsible for illegal tree felling, 
including urban expansion, infrastructure projects, encroachments, illegal mining and 
commercial activities and if so, details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government has reviewed compliance with conditions imposed while 
granting permissions for tree felling under infrastructure, industrial, mining and real estate 
projects and, if so, the number of violations detected, action taken and penalties imposed 
during the said period; and 
(e) whether the Government proposes to strengthen legal framework, monitoring and 
enforcement mechanism to prevent illegal felling of trees and ensure greater accountability 
and if so, details thereof along with the  timeline fixed for its implementation? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (e) Protection of trees and action against illegal felling in urban areas, forest areas and 
peri-urban areas are primarily the responsibility of the respective State Governments/Union 
Territory Administrations under the Indian Forest Act, 1927, the respective State Acts and the 
rules made thereunder. Accordingly, the details regarding the increase or decrease in the 
incidence of illegal tree felling is maintained by the respective State Governments/UT 
Administrations. 
 
However, as per the India State of Forest Report (ISFR) 2023, the forest and tree cover of the 
country is 8,27,356.95 square kilometre, which is 25.17% of the geographical area of the 
country. The forest and tree cover has increased by 1,445.81 square kilometre as compared to 
ISFR 2021. Further, there has been an overall increase of 37,378 square kilometre in forest 
and tree cover during the decade 2013-2023, indicating an increasing trend in the country's 
forest and tree cover. 

In case of illegal felling of trees due to various reasons, the legal actions are taken by State 
Governments and Union Territory Administrations as per applicable Acts and rules made 
thereunder. Further, in case of diversion of forest land, the compensatory afforestation and 
other compliance measures are ensured under the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) 
Adhiniyam, 1980.  There are robust legal framework for protection and management of 
forest and tree resources under the provisions of the Indian Forest Act, 1927, the Van 
(Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980, and the respective State Forest Acts, Tree 
Preservation Acts and Rules. The State Governments/UT Administrations take appropriate 
measures under these legal provisions to prevent illegal felling and protect forest and tree 
resources.

ANSWERED ON MONDAY, 27 JULY, 2026/SHRAVANA 5, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
Loans availed by the State of Haryana

(c)   the details of crop loans, agricultural investment loans and other agricultural loans along with the

(d) whether the Government has launched any new scheme or taken any special initiative to increase the

(e) if so, the details thereof and the benefits likely to accrue to Sonipat and Hisar Lok Sabha Parliamentary

ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY)

ensure interest subvention and timely disbursement of loans to small and marginal farmers across the country, 
including the farmers of Sonipat and Hisar, which inter-alia includes the following:  
i. Setting annual Ground Level Credit (GLC) targets for agriculture and allied sectors, with dedicated targets 
for allied activities such as dairy, fisheries, and animal husbandry.  
ii. Mandating banks under Priority  Sector Lending (PSL) norms to allocate at least 18% of Adjusted Net 
Bank Credit (ANBC)/ Credit Equivalent of Off -Balance Sheet Exposures (CEOBSE) to agriculture, 
including a 10% sub -target for Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs), along with incentive/disinc entive 
mechanisms to improve regional credit flow.  
iii. Providing timely and affordable credit through the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme, which also covers 
allied activities.  
iv. Providing concessional short -term agricultural credit under the Modified Interest S ubvention Scheme 
(MISS) through KCC at an interest rate of 7%, with an additional 3% incentive for prompt repayment, 
reducing the effective interest rate to 4%. 
v. Increasing the collateral -free loan limit from ₹1.60 lakh to ₹2.00 lakh (effective 1 January, 2 025), 
improving credit access for small and marginal farmers.  
vi. Supporting rural infrastructure development through NABARD's Rural Infrastructure Development Fund 
(RIDF) to enhance credit absorption.  
vii. Launching PM Dhan Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PM -DDKY) to imp rove the availability of agricultural 
credit, particularly in districts with low credit disbursement.  
viii. Strengthening Rural Cooperative Banks and Regional Rural Banks through technology upgradation and 
institutional reforms.  
ix. Implementing Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) to provide crop insurance, stabilize farmers' 
incomes, enhance creditworthiness, and mitigate production risks.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF FINANCIAL SERVICES 
LOK SABHA  
UN-STARRED QUESTION NO. 1224 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY , JULY 27, 2026/ SHRA V ANA 5, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
Government Oversight and Sovereign Guarantee for LIC Policyholders 
 
1224. SHRI PARSHOTTAMBHAI RUPALA: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has established a comprehensive mechanism to monitor and  
evaluate the performance, accountability, risk management and governance standards of  
actuarial personnel and investment managers in the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), 
if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether LIC conducts periodic scientific manpower and workload audits across all cadres 
to ensure optimal deployment and operational efficiency, if so,the details thereof; 
(c) the measures taken to reduce the cost per policy while enhancing policyholder returns and 
bonuses; 
(d) whether the Government continues to exercise effective supervisory oversight over LIC’s 
overall functioning, if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) whether all LIC policies continue to be fully backed by the sovereign guarantee of the 
Government of India and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a) & (b) IRDAI has informed that it has framed comprehensive prudential and governance 
framework with the following Regulations / Master Circular which are applicable to all 
insurers, including Life Insurance Corporation of India: 
(1) IRDAI (Actuarial, Finance and Investment Functions of Insurers) Regulations, 2024 
(2) IRDAI (Appointed Actuary) Regulations, 2022 
(3) IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders’ Interests, Operations and Allied Matters of 
Insurers) Regulations, 2024 
(4) Master Circular on Corporate Governance, 2024 
This framework provides for governance arrangements relating to actuarial, finance and 
investment functions, appointment and responsibilities of the Appointed Actuary, Board -
approved policies, internal controls, risk management, investment governance, regu latory 
reporting and supervisory oversight by IRDAI. With the intent to ensure optimal deployment 
and operational efficiency, LIC undertakes review of manpower and workload at periodical 


intervals. This is carried out through review of cadre strength during promotion rounds, 
considering positions to be manned, likely vacancies due to superannuation and elevation, and 
periodic recruitment after careful consideration of activities, future manpower requirem ents, 
and technological/regulatory challenges to ensure efficient customer service.  Employee 
workload and performance are evaluated through a structured appraisal process.  
(c) LIC has undertaken several measures to reduce the cost per policy while enhancing 
policyholders’ returns and bonuses such as rationalization of expenses, increase the number of 
policies, lower withdrawals etc. to attain  economies of scale. LIC has further m odernized its 
Buy-Online-D2C proposal registration platform  with enhanced online integration such as e -
KYC/ CKYC and Bank account verification. Other similar steps involve promotion of paperless 
onboarding through agents portal; online collection of proposal deposits; periodic review of 
Non-Medical limits; realignment of commission structures for certain products in line with 
IRDAI Regulations on Special Surrender Value etc. 
 
(d) LIC is a Board -governed, listed entity regulated by IRDAI under Insurance Act, 1938, 
IRDAI Act, 1999 and the regulations framed thereunder. IRDAI exercises prudential and 
market conduct supervision over LIC in the same manner as over other insurers. Such 
supervision includes monitoring of solvency, actuarial valuation, investments, financial 
reporting, corporate governance, product management, protection of policyholders’ interests, 
market conduct and regulatory compliance through regulatory returns, inspections, supervisory 
reviews and other supervisory processes. 
 
(e) Yes. As per Section 37 of the Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956, the sum assured under 
all policies issued by LIC, together with bonuses already declared, is guaranteed as to payment 
in cash by the Central Government, subject to the provisions contained in Section 14 of the LIC 
Act.

Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the target set for the survey and physical registration of ancient scripts under the      
newly structured Gyan Bharatam Mission framework, district-wise in the country; 
  
(b) whether the Government has integrated advanced Optical Character  Recognition (OCR)  
technology on its portal to process the 18 crore newly  digitised manuscript pages; 
 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d) the manner in which the Government plans to resolve copy-ownership and  intellectual property 
challenges while allowing open public research access to rare religious manuscripts? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM  
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) Under the Gyan Bharatam Mission, National Manuscript Survey was launched across all States and  
Union Territories of the country to identify and document manuscript holdings, repositories and 
custodians representing diverse languages and scripts. However, any district-wise target was not set for 
the survey and physical registration of manuscripts under the Mission. During the survey, more than 
1.19 crore manuscripts have been reported. 
(b) & (c) Gyan Bharatam Web Portal uses AI (Artificial Intelligence) -enabled technologies, including 
Large Language Script Models (LLSM), Optical Character Recognition (OCR), Handwritten Text 
Recognition (HTR), script recognition, semantic search and machine-assisted translation, to provide 
intelligent access to India’s manuscript heritage. 
Gyan Mitram, the AI-powered knowledge interface of the Gyan Bharatam Web Portal uses LLSM, 
OCR, HTR, script recognition, semantic search and machine-assisted translation to enable intelligent 
interpretation, contextualization and exploration of manuscripts by integrating manuscript images, 
transcriptions and translations. 
BharatiyaGPT, features “Manuscript-to-Conversational AI” on Gyan Bharatam Web Portal converting 
manuscript heritage into AI-ready, machine-readable knowledge and provides a multilingual and 

multimodal access, including text, audio and voice-based interaction through its “Talk to Manuscript” 
feature, thereby making India’s knowledge traditions more accessible to scholars, students, researchers 
and the public. 
Pandulipi Darpan is an AI driven tool on Gyan Bharatam Web Portal that enables users to upload or 
select a digitized manuscript image and access AI-assisted script recognition, transliteration and 
translation. 
(d) Access to digitized copies of manuscript is facilitated in accordance with applicable laws and the 
rights of custodians and rights holders. Wherever legally permissible, manuscripts and associated 
metadata may be made available for public and scholarly research through the National Digital 
Repository, while sensitive, restricted or rights-protected materials may be subject to appropriate access 
conditions.

IMPLEMENTATION OF NIVESHAK DIDI INITIATIVE FOR INVESTOR AWARENESS 
 
1226. Shri Arvind Dharmapuri: 
          
 Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
 (a) the objectives and key features of the Niveshak Didi initiative being 
implemented for investor education and financial awareness, particularly among 
women and rural households; 
 (b) the number of Niveshak Didis trained and awareness programmes conducted 
so far, State-wise and district-wise, including in Telangana; 
 (c) the number of citizens, especially women, rural investors, Self Help Groups and 
first-time investors, covered under the initiative during the last three years; 
 (d) whether any programmes have been conducted in Nizamabad, Jagtial and other 
districts of Telangana, if so, the details thereof; and  
 (e) the steps being taken to expand the initiative through post offices, self -help 
groups, Panchayats, Common Service Centres and other local institutions to 
protect small investors from fraud, misleading schemes and unclaimed investment-
related issues? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS AND MINISTRY 
OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(HARSH MALHOTRA) 
 
(a): The Niveshak Didi-Phase 2 initiative, which commenced on 7th April, 2025, aims 
to enhance financial awareness among women in rural and under -served areas, 
promote informed savings and investment decisions, raise awareness on financial 
frauds, advance safe digital financial practices, adopt a community –based “By 
Women, For Women” model, strengthen household financial planning and promote 
financial awareness and banking access to remote regions.  
(b): The State -wise and district -wise details of the number of Niveshak Didis 
trained and the investor awareness programmes conducted so far, including in 
Telangana, are annexed at Annexure.  
 
 

(c):  The number of citizens covered under the initiative during the last three years 
are as under:

Data of categorisation of citizens covered in the programmes is not maintained 
centrally.  
 
 
(d) The information is included in Annexure.  
 
(e) After the success of Phase 1, Investor Education and Protection Fund

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.1227 
ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
  
SKILLING FOR SPACE AND GEOSPATIAL SECTORS 
  
1227. SHRI G M HARISH BALAYOGI: 
  
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)  the details of the skill development/capacity -building programmes implemented in space 
and geospatial sectors, State/UT-wise; 
 
(b)  the details of the persons trained in remote sensing, GIS, satellite data processing and 
geospatial applications during the last three years, programme -wise, State/UT-wise, especially 
in Andhra Pradesh; 
 
(c)  the details of number of training centres, Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) and other 
institutions engaged in such programmes, State/UT, district -wise including Andhra Pradesh, 
particularly Konaseema district; 
 
(d)  whether the Government has assessed the demand for skilled manpower in the space 
and geospatial sectors and identified gaps in availability of trained personnel outside 
established technology hubs, if so, details thereof; 
 
(e)  the details of partnerships with private space entities/start -ups/academic institutions for 
training, internships, apprenticeships and employment in said sectors; 
 
(f)  whether any targeted programmes are proposed by the Government to extend such 
training to rural youth, particularly in Andhra Pradesh and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(g)  the steps taken/proposed to be taken by the Government to link such skill development 
programmes with employment and entrepreneurship opportunities in the space and geospatial 
sectors? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
  
(a) to (c): Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM), the Ministry of Skill 
Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re -skill and up -skill training through 
an extensive network of skill development centres under various schemes to all the sections of 
the society across the country including the state of Andhra Pradesh. The SIM aims at enabling 
youth of India to get future ready, equipped with industry relevant skills. 
  
The Government is actively promoting skill development in the space and geospatial emerging 
technology sectors through flagship schemes of the Ministry of Skill Development and 
Entrepreneurship (MSDE), namely the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana  (PMKVY) and the 
National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS), which impart short -term skilling, up -
skilling, re -skilling through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL), and structured on -the-job 
apprenticeship training in areas such as GIS, spatial data management, drone technology, 
software development, telecommunications, and electronics. Furthermore, to strengthen the 

capacity of Non -Government Entities (NGEs) and academia, IN -SPACe under the Department 
of Space has introduced 11 short -term skill development courses in space technology, under 
which over 1,000 candidates have been successfully trained across the country. 
  
The State/UT -wise number of candidates trained and apprentices engaged in space and 
geospatial related sectors during the last three years as well as the number of training 
centres/establishments under PMKVY and NAPS are provided at Annexure-I and Annexure-II 
respectively. The details of HEIs conducting various space technology courses across the 
country are given at Annexure-III. 
  
(d) to (g): District Skill Committees (DSCs),  established across all States/UTs including 
Andhra Pradesh are mandated with formulating District Skill Development Plans  (DSDPs) to 
support decentralized, grassroots -level skill planning by identifying local employment 
opportunities, skilling demand, and available training infrastructure. Government skill 
programmes are then designed to bridge these identified skill gaps  across sectors. The Sector 
Skill Councils (SSCs), led by industry experts, regularly conduct skill gap studies to assess 
sector-wise skill needs and set competency standards, which guide government interventions to 
align the workforce with industry requirements.   Additionally, the SANKALP (Skill Acquisition 
and Knowledge Awareness for Livelihood Promotion) -supported National Skill Gap Study by 
National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER) provides a standardized, data -driven 
framework to assess skill gaps across seven high -growth sectors. It helps MSDE align skilling 
initiatives with industry demand and future workforce needs. Also, IN -SPACe has carried out an 
assessment of the skilling requirements in areas like space technology, launch vehicle, rockets, 
satellites etc. in consultation with the industry and has undertaken the development of relevant 
course curricula on the basis of the identified needs. 
  
To expand outreach and strengthen the linkage between skilling and employment, the 
Government has been organizing Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Melas  (PMNAMs) 
since June 2022, along with awareness generation, employer outreach, and candidate 
mobilization activities. Through collaboration with employers, industry bodies, educational 
institutions, and Sector Skill Councils, the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) 
facilitates the acquisition of industry -relevant skills and enhances employment and 
entrepreneurship opportunities for youth, including those from rural areas. Further, the faculties 
for short -term skill developments in IN -SPACe are from ISRO, IN -SPACe, Ex -ISRO officers, 
private space entities/start -ups/academic institutions for delivering the lecture and for covering 
practical aspects during the course. 
  
In order to align skill development programs with the industrial requirements in the emerging 
sectors including the space and geospatial sectors, and to facilitate partnerships with private 
entities/academic institutions, to improve the employability of the skilled manpower and 
entrepreneurship opportunities, the following specific steps have been taken by MSDE across 
the country including Andhra Pradesh:  
 
i. National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) has been set up as an 
overarching regulator establishing regulations and standards to ensure quality in the 
Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) space. 
ii. The Awarding Bodies recognised by NCVET are expected to develop the qualifications 
as per the industry demand and map them with the identified occupations as per the 
National Classification of Occupations, 2015 and obtain industry validations. 
iii. NCVET has approved 10,209 qualifications as per the industry requirements, out of 
which 2,975 qualifications are valid and active, and 7,234 qualifications are archived. 
iv. 36 Sector Skill Councils (SSCs), led by industry leaders in the respective sectors, have 
been set up which identify the skill development needs of respective sectors as well as to 
determine skill competency standards. 

v. Directorate General of Training (DGT) under the aegis of MSDE  is implementing Flexi 
MoU Scheme and Dual System of Training (DST) which are meant to provide training to 
ITI students in industrial environment as per their requirements. 
vi. Under PMKVY, the new age/future skills job -roles have been specially aligned with 
Industry 4.0 requirements in areas like AI/ML, Robotics, Mechatronics, Drone 
Technology, etc. for upcoming market demand and industry requirements. 
vii. DGT has introduced new age /future skills courses under CTS to provide training in 
emerging areas such as 5G Network Technician, Artificial Intelligence Programming 
assistant, Cyber Security Assistant, Drone Technician etc. 
viii. DGT has signed MoU with IT Tech companies like IBM, CISCO, Microsoft, AWS etc. to 
ensure industry linkages for the institutes at the state and regional levels. These 
partnerships facilitate the provision of technical and professional skills training in modern 
technologies. 
ix. Indian Institute of Skills (IIS) established at Ahmedabad and Mumbai, in Public Private 
Partnership (PPP) Mode, provide training to create a pool of industry -ready workforce for 
Industry, equipped with cutting-edge technology and hands-on training. 
x. Kaushal Melas and Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Melas (PMNAMs) are 
organised to facilitate the placements and apprenticeship opportunities to the certified 
candidates. 
xi. IN-SPACe has conducted two editions of IN -SPACe CANSAT India Student competition 
and one edition of IN -SPACe model rocketry student India competition, which resulted in 
inculcation of space technology interest among the college students and created ample 
employment opportunities. 
xii. IN-SPACe is also providing internship and Immersion opportunities to college students to 
empower them with relevant skill for the space sector.

LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1229 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
MEDICAL CARE FOR INSURED WORKERS 
 
1229. SHRI ARUN BHARTI: 
 
         Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)whether the proactive upgradation of Employee's State Insurance 
(ESI) hospitals and dispensaries has successfully ensured premium 
medical care for insured workers in the Jamui Constituency; 
(b)if so, the details of the central financial allocations utilized to 
modernize the medical  equipment, diagnostic labs and bed 
capacities of ESI facilities in the region during 2025-26; 
(c) whether the said infrastructural upgrades have permanently 
reduced the need for industrial laborers to travel to distant private 
hospitals for specialized emergency treatments and if so, the  
details thereof; 
(d) the total number of insured workers and their dependent family 
members who successfully received free, cashless medical care at 
local level during the last year; and 
(e) the details of the future initiatives planned by the Government to 
deploy mobile ESI medical vans to provide on-site health checkups 
directly at the factory premises for industrial workers? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (e) As per the Employees’ State Insurance (ESI) norms, 
minimum 3000 Insured Persons (IPs) are required for opening of an 
ESI dispensary and minimum 50000 IPs are required for setting up of 
a 100 Bedded ESI Hospital. As on 31.03.2025, there are only 1,149 IPs 
available in the Jamui district. Hence, it does not meet the prescribed 
norms for setting up an ESI dispensary or hospital. However, IPs and 
their family members in Jamui districts are receiving cashless benefit 
through tie -ups hospitals and ESI Model Hospi tal Phulwarisharif, 
Patna and ESI Medical College Bihta. 
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
  At present, there are no  future initiatives planned by the 
Government to deploy mobile ESI medical vans to provide on -site 
health check -ups directly at the factory premises for industrial 
workers. However, health check -ups are being conducted through 
camps at factories and Insured Persons cluster areas, with basic 
diagnostic and treatment facilities. In addition, annual health check-
ups have also been initiated at all ESI hospitals, recently.
