GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION AND LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1230 
ANSWERED ON 27/07/2026 
 
Separate Toilets for Girl Students at School Level 
 
1230.  Shri Gurmeet Singh Meet Hayer: 
 
  Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number and percentage of Government Schools in the country equipped with separate 
functional toilets for girls and Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM) facilities, including 
incinerators, State-wise;  
 
(b) the details of annual dropout rates of girl students segregated in primary, upper-primary and 
secondary levels during the last three years, State-wise; and  
 
(c) whether any central impact assessment has been conducted linking inadequate sanitation 
infrastructure with female dropouts and if so, the key findings thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) The Department of School Education and Literacy (DoSEL), Ministry of Education has 
developed the Unified District Information System for Education Plus (UDISE+) system to 
record data on indicators of school education provided by all the States and Union Territories. 
As per UDISE+ 2025 -26, the number and percentage of Government Schools i n the country 
equipped with separate functional toilets for girls is at Annexure-I.   
The Department of School Education and Literacy (DoSEL), Ministry of Education, is 
implementing the scheme of Samagra Shiksha, effective from 2018-19, for universalization of 
quality education throughout the country in coordination with the States and UTs.  In order to 
bridge the social and gender gaps, under Samagra Shiksha , support for installation of sanitary 
pad vending machines and incinerators  among others are provided, based on the proposals 
received from the State/UT Governments as a part of Annual Work Plan and Budget 
(AWP&B).   
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare implements the 'Scheme for Promotion of 
Menstrual Hygiene' under Rashtriya Kishor Srvasthya Karyakram (RKSK). The objectives of  
the scheme are to increase awareness among adolescent girls on menstrual hygiene. to increase 
access to sanitary napkins by adolescent girls and to promote safe disposal of sanitary napkins 
in an environmentally  friendly manner. Under this scheme sanitary napkins are provided to 
adolescent girls by ASHAs using the platforms of schools and community. It is supported by  

the National Health Mission through the State Programme Implementation Plans (PIP) route, 
based on the proposals received from the States/UTs. 
As per the Health Management In formation System (HMIS), the menstrual hygiene  
interventions under NHM reached 53.9 lakhs adolescent girls every month in FY 2025 -26 
through distribution of sanitary napkins and awareness activities. 
The National Menstrual Hygiene Policy for School-Going Girls, which provides an 
overarching framework to promote awareness, ensure access to safe and affordable menstrual 
absorbents, strengthen WASH infrastructure, and enable sa le disposal mechanisms through 
convergence with concerned Ministries/Departments and States/UTs has been formulated as 
well. 
(b) As per UDISE+ 2024 -25, State/UT -wise dropout rate among girls  calculated at 
primary, Upper Primary and secondary level of education is at Annexure -II.  
(c) As per report titled ‘Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)’ for the year 2023 -24, 
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), the major reasons for drop-out 
of female are to supplement household income, to attend domestic chores,  education not 
considered necessary by the parents, etc.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1231 
ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
  
INDUSTRY-ALIGNED SKILL DEVELOPMENT  
  
†1231  SHRI DHARMENDRA YADAV: 
 
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP  be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware that despite various skill development programmes in 
the country, a large number of youths are unable to secure employment commensurate with their 
training qualifications; 
 
(b)  if so, the details of the youth trained, certified and gainfully employed under major schemes 
(such as PMKVY etc.) functioning under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship 
during the last five years and the current year, State/UT-wise; 
  
(c)  whether the Government has conducted any assessment regarding the gap between the 
quality of skill training, industry requirements and employability, if so, the major findings thereof; 
and 
  
(d)  the steps taken/being taken by the Government to enhance the employability of the youth, 
strengthen industry -aligned training and increase the effectiveness of skill development 
programmes? 
   
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
  
(a) to (d):  As per the latest estimates of the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), conducted 
by the National Sample Survey Office, the unemployment rate on usual status for person of age 
15-59 years has decreased from 6.5 per cent in 2017-18 to 3.4 per cent in 2025.  
 
To improve the employability of youth of the country, the Ministry of Skill Development and 
Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up- skill training through an extensive network 
of skill development centres/institutes under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas 
Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme 
(NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), to all 
the sections of the society across the country. The SIM aims at enabling youth of India to get 
future-ready, equipped with industry-relevant skills. 
 
The details of the beneficiaries trained and certified under various schemes under MSDE during 
the last five years and the current year up to 30.06.2026, State/UT-wise are given at Annexure. 
 
Under PMKVY, placements were tracked in the Short-Term Training (STT) component in the first 
three versions of the Scheme - PMKVY 1.0, PMKVY 2.0 and PMKVY 3.0, implemented from 
FY2015-16 to FY 2021 -22. Under PMKVY 1.0 to 3.0 a total of 1.11 Crore candidate s were 
certified, out of which 24.38 lakhs were reported placed under the STT component of the scheme. 

Further, under PMKVY 4.0, the focus is to empower the trained candidates to choose their varied 
career paths, and they are suitably oriented for the same.  
 
PMKVY: An independent third-party impact evaluation of the PMKVY 4.0 has been conducted by 
Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM), an autonomous Institution of 
Ministry of Finance, Government of India. As per the 2025 report, PMKVY training has contributed 
to a measurable shift in employment outcomes for STT candidates. The combined share of 
employed and self-employed STT respondents increased from 26.6% prior to training to 45.4% 
after PMKVY training, reflecting an 18.8 percentage poin t increase. Income -related outcomes 
also show positive movement, with 41.4% of STT candidates and 48.9% of RPL candidates 
reporting an increase in income following training and certification. Overall, PMKVY 4.0 has 
significantly expanded access to formal s kill training and certification and has generated 
measurable improvements in skill confidence, employment participation, and income outcomes 
for a substantial proportion of beneficiaries. 
   
JSS: A third-party evaluation of the Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) Scheme was conducted by the 
Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management, an autonomous Institution of the Ministry 
of Finance, Government of India, in 2025 to assess the scheme’s out reach, effectiveness and 
livelihood outcomes. The evaluation highlighted significant achievements of the scheme, with 
33.94 lakh individuals enrolled, of whom 32 lakh  were trained and 31.52 lakh certified, reflecting 
an overall success rate of 99 percent. Women constituted a dominant 82 percent share of total 
participants, while 73 percent beneficiaries belonged to marginalized sections, including SC/ST 
(36 percent) and OBC (37 percent). The livelihood impact has been noteworthy, with 90 percent 
alumni utilizing acquired skills for income generation, 82 percent becoming economically engaged 
within six months of training, and 60 percent of previously non-earning individuals starting to earn 
post-training. The average monthly income of beneficiaries recorded a four-fold increase. 
  
NAPS: A third -party evaluation study of Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Promotion 
Scheme (PMNAPS-2) from FY 2022 -23 to FY 2025 -26 (Data up to 30 th November 2025) was 
conducted by the Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM),  an 
autonomous Institution of Ministry of Finance, Government of India. As per the report, PMNAPS 
2 achieved significant scale during the evaluation period, engaging 34.69 lakh apprentices against 
a cumulative target of 46 lakh, translating into an overall achievement of approximately 75 
percent. The institutionalization of DBT has improved financial transparency and predictability. 
Cumulative DBT disbursem ent exceeded ₹1,094 crore, with annual disbursement rising from 
₹327.2 crore in FY 2023–24 to ₹500.16 crore in FY 2024–25. 
   
To enhance the employability of the youth, strengthen industry-aligned training and increase the 
effectiveness of skill development programs, the following steps have been taken by MSDE:  
  
i. National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) has been set up as an 
overarching regulator, establishing regulations and standards to ensure quality in the 
Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) space.  
ii. The Awarding Bodies recognized by NCVET are expected to develop the qualifications as 
per industry demand and map them with the identified occupations as per the National 
Classification of Occupations, 2015 and obtain industry validations.  
iii. 36 Sector Skill Councils (SSCs), led by industry leaders in the respective sectors, have 
been set up which identify the skill development needs of respective sectors as well as to 
determine skill competency standards.  
iv. Directorate General of Training (DGT) under the aegis of MSDE is implementing Flexi MoU 
Scheme and Dual System of Training (DST) which are meant to provide training to ITI 
students in industrial environment as per their requirements.  
v. Under PMKVY, the new age/future skills job-roles have been specially aligned with Industry 
4.0 requirements in areas like AI/ML, Robotics, Mechatronics, Drone Technology, etc. for 
upcoming market demand and industry requirements. 

vi. DGT has introduced new age /future skills courses under CTS to provide training in 
emerging areas such as 5G Network Technician, Artificial Intelligence Programming 
assistant, Cyber Security Assistant, Drone Technician etc.  
vii. DGT has signed MoU with IT Tech companies like IBM, CISCO, Microsoft, AWS etc. to 
ensure industry linkages for the institutes at the state and regional levels. These 
partnerships facilitate the provision of technical and professional skills training in mod ern 
technologies.  
viii. Indian Institute of Skills (IIS) established at Ahmedabad and Mumbai, in Public Private 
Partnership (PPP) Mode, provide training to create a pool of industry -ready workforce for 
Industry, equipped with cutting-edge technology and hands-on training.  
ix. Kaushal Melas and Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Melas (PMNAMs) are 
organised to facilitate the placements and apprenticeship opportunities to the certified 
candidates. 
x. Government has launched PM -SETU (Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability 
Transformation through Upgraded ITIs), a centrally sponsored scheme with an investment 
of Rs.60,000 crore. The scheme envisages the upgradation of 1,000 Government ITIs 
across the country in a hub-and-spoke model comprising 200 hub ITIs and 800 spoke ITIs. 
PM-SETU focuses on improving employability outcomes through industry-led governance, 
and indirectly supports self -employment and entrepreneurship by enabling learners 
(including early-stage enterprises and first-time entrepreneurs) to acquire industry-relevant 
skills, gain exposure to real work environments, and access career guidance, placement 
support, and self -employment support through strengthened institutional systems and 
industry linkages.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION AND LITERACY 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1232 
ANSWERED ON 27/07/2026 
Introduction of AI Education in Punjab  
 
1232. Shri Charanjit Singh Channi: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken cognizance of the initiative to introduce Artificial Intelligence-
based curriculum in Government schools of Punjab, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether any assistance has been sought or provided  under centrally sponsored education schemes 
for implementation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digital learning programmes in the State, if so, 
the details thereof; 
(c) the details of funds allocated and released for digital infrastructure, smart clas srooms and teacher 
training in Punjab during the last three years; and 
(d) the steps taken to ensure equitable access to AI education for students in rural and economically 
weaker areas? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (d): The Government of Punjab has informed that Artificial Intelligence (AI) and other 
emerging technologies are being introduced through digital literacy initiatives, coding activities, ICT 
enabled learning and teacher capacity -building programmes in all Government schools. Al related 
awareness and foundational concepts are being integrated through available digital learning platforms 
and innovation-based activities in accordance with the curriculum and guidelines issued from time to 
time. 
         The Department of School Education & Literacy is implementing the Centrally Sponsored 
Schemes of Samagra Shiksha and PM SHRI  in partnership with States and UTs. Financial assistance 
is provided to all States and UTs for various components for im plementation of the interventions as 
per norms. Accordingly, the annual plans are prepared by the States and UTs based on their 
requirements and priority and this is reflected in their respective Annual Work Plan and Budget 
(AWP&B). These plans are then ap praised and approved by Project Approval Board (PAB) in 
consultation with the States and UTs as per the programmatic and financial norms of the scheme. 
The Proposal of the state of Punjab for implementation of AI based learning, AI learning kits 
and teache r training in Government schools  has been  approved under PM SHRI and Samagra 
Shiksha for FY2026-27.  
As informed by the Government of Punjab, the funds allocated and released for digital 
infrastructure and smart classrooms in Punjab during the last three years is as follows:

A comprehensive initiative called PM eVidya was initiated as part of Atma Nirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan 
on 17th May, 2020, which unifies all efforts related to digital/online/on-air education to enable multi-
mode access to education across the countr y. States/UTs collaborate with NCERT to utilise, monitor 
and evaluate the effectiveness of these initiatives as per their requirements. NCERT also provides 
regular guidance/ feedback to States/UTs on the quality of these initiatives. The PM eVidya initiati ve 
includes 200 DTH TV channels and 400 Radio channels to enable all States/UTs to provide 
supplementary education in various Indian languages for Classes 1 -12. As part of PM eVidya, 5 
Channels (PB PM eVidya 143 to 147) have been allocated to the state of Punjab. Content on 
Artificial Intelligence and Expert Systems in Punjabi has been made available by the State. 
    Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing (DIKSHA) is a One Nation, One Digital 
platform for providing quality e -content for school educat ion in States/UTs along with QR coded 
Energised Textbooks (ETBs) for all grades. The platform supports both online and offline access, 
enabling learners to download content and continue learning without internet connectivity, ensuring 
equitable access to A I education for students in rural and economically weaker areas. Currently, 
DIKSHA holds 59 courses on AI and Digital Learning with 9.4+ lakh enrolments. 
      The Government of India, in the Budget 2025, has announced provision of broadband 
connectivity to all Government Secondary schools in rural areas, under the ‘BharatNet’ project by 
BSNL to enhance digital infrastructure in remote areas in a phased manner i ncluding 1,200 
Government Rural Secondary schools in Punjab. 
 
     To ensure equitable access to AI and digital education, especially for students in rural and 
economically weaker areas, the State has undertaken measures like strengthening ICT infrastructu re 
and Smart Classrooms in Government schools under Samagra Shiksha, providing access to digital 
learning resources through DIKSHA and other e -content platforms, organising capacity -building 
programmes for teachers on digital pedagogy and emerging technolo gies, promoting coding, 
innovation, STEM education and AI awareness through school -level activities and innovation 
programmes. 
 
      Further, The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship launched a national level 
initiative SOAR (Skilling for AI  Readiness), which aims to embed AI awareness and foundational 
skills among school students (Classes 6 –12) including students in rural and economically weaker 
sections and to build AI literacy among educators. SOAR comprises three progressive 15 -hour 
modules for students —AI to be Aware, AI to Acquire, and AI to Aspire —and one independent 45 -
hour module for teachers titled AI for Educators. The program introduces concept s such as AI basics, 
generative AI, AI in daily life, programming fundamentals, ethics, cybersecurity and future career 
opportunities.

(a) the objectives of the experiential learning programmes offered  
through the MY Bharat platform, and the manner in which these are 
bridging the gap between academic education, and practical and 
real-world experience; 
(b) the details of the various experiential learning programmes 
currently available on the said platfor m through Government 
departments, academic institutions and businesses;

ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS 
[DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA] 
(a) The objective of the Experiential Learning Programmes (ELPs) 
offered through the MY Bharat platform is to provide youth with 
structured, short-term, hands-on learning opportunities in real work 
environments with Government Departments, public institutions and 
partner organisations. These programmes are designed to 
strengthen the application of classroom knowledge in real -world 
settings, develop functional and professional competencies, and 
familiarise participants with the  functioning of public institutions 
and community-based initiatives. 
The programmes bridge the gap between academic education and 
practical experience by enabling participants to undertake 
structured assignments under the guidance of host organisations. 
Participants apply concepts learnt through formal education in 
actual work environments, observe institutional processes, and gain 
practical exposure through field and office -based activities. Each 
programme has defined learning objectives, assigned tasks, 
supervision and completion requirements to ensure structured 
learning. The programmes cover sectors such as healthcare, postal 
services, agriculture, broadcasting, road safety, public distribution, 
governance and community development. On successful 
completion, participants receive a jointly validated digital 
certificate issued through the MY Bharat portal. 
(b) to (d) MY Bharat offers Experiential Learning Programmes (ELPs) 
in collaboration with Government Departments, public institutions, 
academic instituti ons and partner organisations through the MY 
Bharat portal. Major programmes include India Post ELP with the 
Department of Posts; Jan Aushadhi ELP with the Pharmaceuticals & 
Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI); Seva Se Seekhen ELP with 
State and Distric t Health Departments; Public Distribution System 
(PDS) ELP with Departments of Food and Civil Supplies; Sadak 
Suraksha Mitra ELP with the Ministry of Road Transport & 
Highways, CoERS -IIT Madras and SaveLIFE Foundation; Radio 
Production and Presentation ELP  with Prasar Bharati and the 
National Academy of Broadcasting & Multimedia (NABM); Farmer 
Producer Organisation (FPO) ELP with Farmer Producer 
Organisations; Youth Engagement with Senior Citizens at Care 

Page 3 of 4 
 
Homes ELP; and the Semiconductor Training Programme with the 
Centre for Nano Science and Engineering (CeNSE), Indian Institute 
of Science, Bengaluru, and the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. These 
programmes cover sectors such as healthcare, postal services, food 
security, agriculture, broadcasting, road safety,  semiconductor 
technology, elderly care and community development, with 
programme duration and implementation modalities varying 
according to programme requirements. 
Since the launch of the MY Bharat platform, more than 1.22 lakh 
youth have enrolle d in abo ut 2 5,000 Experiential Learning 
Programmes and have been issued digital certificates through the 
MY Bharat portal. The State/UT-wise details are at Annexure-I. 
(e) The Experiential Learning Programmes (ELPs) are implemented 
through a standard framework on the MY Bharat portal. Partner 
organisations publish programme details, including objectives, 
eligibility, duration, location and activities. Interested youth apply 
through the portal, and applications are scrutinised by the 
respective host organisations. S elected participants undergo 
orientation and undertake assigned activities under the supervision 
of the host organisation. Attendance, participation and completion 
of assigned tasks are monitored throughout the programme. Upon 
successful completion of the prescribed requirements, the host 
organisation verifies completion on the MY Bharat portal, following 
which a jointly validated digital certificate is generated. 
MY Bharat provides the digital platform, operational framework, 
programme monitoring and certi ficate generation, while the 
respective host organisations are responsible for participant 
selection, supervision, attendance, verification of completion and 
certification through the MY Bharat portal. NSS Programme Officers 
and Placement Officers facilita te awareness, mobilisation and 
guidance of eligible students for participation in suitable 
programmes.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1234 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY , JULY 27, 2026 
SHRAVANA 5, 1948 (SAKA) 
SALIENT FEATURES OF CORPORATE LAWS (AMENDMENT BILL), 2026 
QUESTION 
 
1234. Dr. Bhola Singh: 
 
Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the steps taken by the Government since 2014 to decriminalise offences 
under the Companies Act, 2013 and the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 
2008;  
 
(b) the salient features of the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 
relating to compliance relief for companies;  
 
(c) the measures taken by the Government to strengthen the fast -track 
merger framework; and  
 
(d) the expected impact on ease of doing business ? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFAIRS AND 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD, TRANSPORT AND 
HIGHWAYS 
[SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA]  
 
(a): In keeping with the Government’s objective of providing greater ease 
of doing business to law abiding corporates, process of de -criminalization 
of technical & procedural violations under Companies Act, 2013 (CA -13) 
and Limited Liability Partnerships (LLPs) was carried out in phased manner 
since 2014-15. The details are at Annexure-I. 
(b): The salient features of the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 
relating to compliance relief for companies are at Annexure-II. 
(c) & (d): The Government has taken steps to expand, rationalize, and 
strengthen the fast -track merger (FTM) framework under Section 233 
of the Companies Act, 2013 to encourage ease of doing business and 
provide a cost -effective, administrative mechanism for corporate 
reorganizations. The details are at Annexure-III. 
 

Annexure-I 
 
Annexure-I to the Lok  Sabha Unstarred Q. No. 1234 part (a ) to be 
answered on 27th July, 2026 
 
In the first phase, through the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2019, 16 
compoundable offences under the CA -13 were decriminalized and shifted 
to an In-house Adjudication Mechanism. 
In the second phase, through the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2020, 35 
more compoundable offences under the CA -13 were de -criminalized. In 
addition, through this amendment, in case of 11 compoundable offences, 
provisions for imprisonment were removed and only fines were retained.  
Further, 12 offences have been decriminalized in LLP Act, 2008 through 
the Limited Liability Partnership (Amendment) Act, 2021.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

Annexure-II 
 
Annexure-II to the Lok  Sabha Unstarred Q. No. 1234 part  (b) to be 
answered on 27th July, 2026 
 
• Decriminalisation of various procedural defaults under the Companies 
Act and the LLP Act by replacing criminal provisions with civil 
penalties; 
 
 
• Simplification of procedures relating to mergers and amalgamations 
through rationalisation of approval thresholds for fast -track mergers 
and enabling filing of applications before a single bench of the National 
Company Law Tribunal having jurisdiction over the transferee 
company; 
 
 
• Providing further relaxations for small companies by providing 
exemption from mandatory Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), 
requirements related to auditor appointment for prescribed class of 
small companies, reduction in additional fees, reduction in number of 
Board meetings, increase in upper threshold for the definition of small 
companies etc. 
 
• Simplification of procedures relating to voluntary strike -off of 
companies to facilitate quicker and simpler closure or voluntary exit 
for companies; 
 
• Relaxations in CSR requirements through revision of eligibility 
thresholds and enhancing timelines for transfer of unspent amounts to 
a separate bank account relating to ongoing project and revising 
eligibility threshold with regard to constitution of CSR committees; 
 
• Facilitating companies and limited liability partnerships operating in 
International Financial Services Centres by allowing them to issue and 
maintain share capital in foreign currency as permitted by the 
International Financial Services Centres Authority; 
 
• Enabling companies to hold Annual General Meetings and Extraordinary 
General Meetings through video conferencing or other audio visual 
means with requirement for holding at least one Annual General 
Meeting in physical mode within a specified period; 
 
• Replacement of certain affidavits required under th e Act with self -
declarations;  
 
 
 
• Recognising new forms of instruments linked to the value of share 
capital for executive compensation. 

 
Annexure-III 
 
Annexure-III to the Lok  Sabha Unstarred Q. No. 1234 part (c) & (d) to 
be answered on 27th July, 2026 
 
 
• Originally, only mergers between two or more small companies, or 
between a holding company and its wholly-owned subsidiary company 
were allowed under this route.  
 
• Vide Companies (Compromises, Arrangements and Amalgamations) 
Amendment Rules, 2021, mergers between start -ups, and between 
small companies and start-ups were also included in the scope.  
 
• In 2024, cross -border reverse flipping under the fast-track merger  
framework was allowed, which permitted a foreign holding company  
to directly merge into its wholly-owned subsidiary in India.  
 
 
• In 2025, the eligibility criteria of FTM was further widened to include 
merger between unlisted companies (other than section 8 company), 
provided that the aggregate outstanding borrowings (including bank 
loans, debentures, and public deposits) of each com pany does not 
exceed Rs. 200 crores. This  also allows for intra -group restructuring 
between a holding company and its subsidiaries, as well as between 
fellow subsidiaries. 
 
• Further, there are provisions for deemed approval under the FTM 
framework to ensure that these mergers are approved within the 60 
days timeline.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TOURISM  
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.†1235 
ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
DEVELOPMENT OF TOURISM IN AMROHA 
 
†1235. SHRI KANWAR SINGH TANWAR: 
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the progress made in developing Amroha district, Uttar 
Pradesh as a heritage, spiritual and cultural tourism destination by 
integrating historical sites, ancient temples Shah Vilayat Dargah, Tigri 
Dham, traditional handicraft centres and other local cultural attractions 
with tourism infrastructure, tourist amenities, digital promotion and 
heritage tourism circuits; 
(b) the details of the works relating to tourism infrastructure, village 
development and publicity/ promotion undertaken in the  said district 
under various central Government schemes; 
(c) the details of the funds sanctioned, released and utilised for tourism 
development in the said district during the last three years;  
(d) the details of the progress made in terms of the number of tourists, 
generation of local employment development of tourism facilities and 
strengthening of heritage-based tourism in the said district; and 
(e) the details of the projects identified by the Government for promoting 
sustainable heritage and cultural tourism in the said district? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM                 (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (e): Identification, development and promotion of tourism destinations 
and products including heritage, spiritual and cultural is primarily undertaken 
by the concerned State Government (SG)/Union Territory Administration (UTA).  
 
However, the Ministry of Tourism through its schemes of ‘Swadesh 
Darshan (SD)’, ‘Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0)’, ‘Challenge Based Destination 

Development (CBDD)’ – a sub-scheme of SD2.0, and ‘Pilgrimage Rejuvenation 
and Spiritual, Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD)’ complements the 
efforts of tourism infrastructure development by extending financial 
assistance to the State Governments/UT Admi nistrations; subject to 
adherence to scheme guidelines, submission of Detailed Project Reports 
(DPRs) by them, availability of funds, Government directions, inter -se priority 
etc. The projects are executed by the SG/UT implementing agencies and after 
completion, Operation and Management of created assets is also undertaken 
by the concerned SG/UTA.  
 
In addition, Government of India under its initiative for ‘Special 
Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) – Development of Iconic 
Tourist Centres to Global Scale’ scheme, has also provided financial 
assistance to the States including Uttar Pra desh in the year 2024 -25 for 
development of tourism projects. 
 
Sanctioning of project under applicable schemes is a continuous process 
and Ministry of Tourism has sanctioned multiple projects under aforesaid 
schemes in the state of Uttar Pradesh; with an overall objective to enhance 
tourism experience and resulting in  employment generation at destinations. 
Details of the projects sanctioned under SD, SD2.0, CBDD, SASCI and 
PRASHAD schemes in the state of Uttar Pradesh is annexed. 
 
In addition, Ministry of Tourism promotes India as a holistic tourism 
destination including sustainable, heritage and culture tourism. Ministry also 
promotes various tourism destinations including those located in the state of 
Uttar Pradesh through various  medium such as social media, websites, 
participation in fairs and exhibitions etc.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1236 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
Tree Felling and Timber Transit Framework 
 
1236.  THIRU DR. S JAGATHRATCHAKAN: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of nature and extent of variations identified by the Government between Central 
guidelines and State-level regulations relating to tree felling and timber transit and the manner in 
which such variations affect agroforestry development, farmer participation and movement of 
farm-grown timber across regions; 
(b) the details of actions initiated by the Government for promoting greater convergence between 
regulatory provisions applicable at the Central and State levels and addressing inconsistencies that 
create administrative and operational difficulties; 
(c) the details of outcomes achieved through efforts aimed at simplifying approval procedures, 
reducing compliance requirements and improving regulatory clarity for stakeholders engaged in 
agroforestry activities; and 
(d) the institutional mechanisms put in place by the Government for facilitating coordination with 
States, including Tamil Nadu on the matters relating to agroforestry regulation and timber transit? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE 
CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d) : The felling of trees and issuance of transit permits for timber grown under agroforestry 
is regulated by the respective State Governments under the provisions of the Indian Forest Act, 
1927, State-specific Forest Acts, State specific Tree management Acts, rules made thereunder, and 
orders of the Hon’ble Courts. The list of exempted tree species, as well as the procedures and 
documentation required for obtaining felling and transit permits, vary from State to State, depending 
upon the applicable State-specific Acts, rules and directions of the Hon’ble Courts. 
 
The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has issued various guidelines and 
advisories to States and Union Territories for liberalising the transit and felling regulations for 
promoting agroforestry. 
 
The Ministry has revised the Wood Based Industries (Establishment and Regulation) guidelines in 
2022 to liberalize the regulations relating to setting up of Wood-based Industries using species 
grown under agroforestry. 
 
The Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education (ICFRE) has been continuously pursuing 
tree improvement programs to promote agroforestry. So far, ICFRE has released 69 varieties and 

clones that are being widely planted by farmers, forest departments, forest development corporations 
and wood-based industries in agro forestry and social forestry programmes. 
 
During May 2022, the Central Government amended the export policy to make the export of bamboo 
charcoal "Free", to create greater value addition within the bamboo sector, and improve the 
profitability and livelihood opportunities associated with bamboo-based industries. 
 
The Ministry, during March 2023 complied and released a book on ‘FAQ on Agroforestry’ which 
serves as a guide to farmers and field practitioners by providing cultivation practices of 36 selective 
tree species suitable for agroforestry systems and home gardens. The Ministry has also released 
booklets on cultivation practices for four commercially important tree species, namely Agarwood, 
Sandalwood, Red sanders and rosewood to promote their cultivation by farmers and tree growers. 
 
During December 2023, the Ministry launched the National Transit Pass System (NTPS), a pan-
India, online system, to streamline and digitize the issuance of transit permits for timber, bamboo 
and other forest produce. It facilitates seamless movement of forest produce across State and Union 
Territory borders through a single digital platform, reduces procedural delays and promotes ease of 
doing business. The system enables online issuance of transit passes and No Objection Certificates 
(NOCs), thereby improving transparency, efficiency and traceability in the movement of forest 
produce. As of now, 4,36,258 Transit Passes have been issued throughout the Country including 
Tamil Nadu. 
 
The Ministry, in June 2025, issued the Model Rules for “Felling of Trees in Agricultural Land” for 
consideration and adoption by the States, with the objective of encouraging and promoting 
agroforestry among farmers. The Model Rules are advisory in nature and provide a framework for 
States and Union Territories to simplify and streamline the procedures for felling and transit of trees 
grown on private agricultural lands, while promoting greater uniformity, transparency, and ease of 
doing business in the agroforestry sector. 
 
The Ministry regularly engages with States and Union Territories, including Tamil Nadu, through 
consultations, workshops and capacity-building programmes to facilitate and promote agroforestry.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1237 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
Ban on Single-Use Plastic 
 
1237.   SHRI ANIL YESHWANT DESAI: 
SHRI RAMVIR SINGH BIDHURI: 
SHRI SANJAY UTTAMRAO DESHMUKH: 
SHRI SANJAY HARIBHAU JADHAV: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware about the increasing level of pollution in cities due to 
various reasons; if so, the details thereof, Sources-wise; 
(b)  the standing of country in international index of pollution along with the steps taken by the 
Government to control the use of plastic and other polluting materials in the country; 
(c) whether the ban on plastic by the market is effective, if so the status of the ban on single-
use plastic bags across the country along with the data of prosecution against the violations of 
the rules including shop keepers and common consumers; 
(d) the reasons for open  and uninterrupted use of plastic in the national capital of Delhi in 
almost all the weekly markets along with the steps taken to check this practice; and 
(e) whether the Government has provided any financial or technical assistance to the States for 
the effective implementation of the Plastic Waste Management and if so, the details thereof, 
State-wise along with the details of any alternatives to plastic bags found by the Government 
or Non-Government Agencies? 
   
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
(a) to (e):  The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change notified Plastic Waste 
Management Amendment Rules, 2021, on 12th August 2021, prohibiting identified Single Use 
Plastic (SUP) items, which have low utility and high littering potential, with effect from 1 July 
2022. The notification also prohibits manufacture, import, stocking, distribution, sale and use 
of plastic carry bags having thickness less than one hundred and twenty microns with effect 
from 31 December 2022. Non-woven plastic carry bags of less than 60 gram per sqm (GSM) 
are also prohibited from 30th September 2021. 
 
States and Union Territories have been asked to undertake regular enforcement drives 
to implement ban on identified single use plastic items and on plastic carry bags having 

thickness less than one hundred twenty microns covering fruit and vegetable markets, 
wholesale markets, local markets, flower vendors, units manufacturing plastic carry bags etc. 
As per details provided by SPCBs/PCCs and details available at SUP compliance monitoring 
portal, a total of 8,62,356 inspections has been conducted, and 1990 tonnes of banned single 
use plastic items have been seized and a total of Rs. 19.85 crores of fine have been levied from 
July, 2022, till January, 2026. 
The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has also notified the Guidelines 
on the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) for plastic packaging vide Plastic Waste 
Management Amendment Rules, 2022, on 16th February, 2022. The Guidelines stipulate 
mandatory targets on EPR, recycling of plastic packaging waste, reuse of rigid plastic 
packaging and use of recycled plastic content. Under Swachh Bharat Mission Urban 2.0 (SBM-
U 2.0) implemented by Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and Swachh Bharat Mission 
(Grameen) phase II, implemented by Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, central 
assistance is provided to States/UTs for solid waste management including plastic waste 
management.  
Further, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) prevents and 
control air and water pollution through enactment of Water (Prevention and Control of 
Pollution) Act, 1974, Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 and Environment 
(Protection) Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Central Pollution 
Control Board and State Pollution Control Boards/Pollution Control Committees undertake 
monitoring and enforcement activities as per mandate.  
 
To provide better air quality in urban areas, the Government has launched the National Clean 
Air Programme (NCAP) as a long-term, time-bound, national level strategy to address air 
pollution in 130 Non-Attainment and million plus cities/urban agglomerations in 24 States/UTs 
including North India. MoEFCC conducts Swachh Vayu Survekshan annually to rank 130 
cities, which are covered under National Clean Air Programme and the results are available on  
website of CPCB at https://prana.cpcb.gov.in/ncapServices/robust/fetchFilesFrom 
Drive/Swachh_Vayu_Survekshan_2025_Result.pdf.  Further, CPCB has formulated 
Comprehensive Environmental Pollution Index (CEPI), which is a rational number (ranging 
from 0 to 100) to characterize environmental quality at a given industrial area following 
algorithm of pollution source, pathway and receptor. The industrial area having aggregated 
CEPI scores 70 and above are considered as Critically Polluted Areas (CPAs), whereas CEPI 
scores ≥60 and <70 are considered as Severely Polluted Areas (SPAs) and CEPI scores less 
than 60 are considered as Other Polluted Areas (OPAs). Worldwide ranking of cities for 
pollution levels is not being conducted by official authority.

1240. Shri Bapi Haldar: 
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of funds sanctioned and released under various Central

(b) whether the Government  has received any proposal for development

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.1244 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
Digitisation of Tulu and Coastal Kannada Manuscripts and Archives 
 
1244. Shri Captain Brijesh Chowta: 
 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
a) whether the Government has reviewed digitisation of Tulu and Coastal Kannada manuscripts and 
archives and the proposals, institutions and locations covered in Dakshina Kannada; 
b) the details of funds sanctioned, released and utilised along with appraisal stage, beneficiaries, 
works and outputs, scheme-wise; 
c) the details of documentation, eligibility, conservation, capacity and State-level action gaps; and 
d) the details of the technical-assistance, appraisal and implementation timeline? 
 
 
   ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM 
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) During the National Manuscript Survey launched in March, 2026 under the Gyan Bharatam Mission 
(GBM), repositories in Dakshina Kannada district of Karnataka preserving manuscripts in Tulu, 
Kannada and Sanskrit have been identified. However, w.r.t. review of digitization of archives, National 
Archives of India (NAI) has informed that there is no such development. 
Based on the survey findings, eligible repositories having manuscripts, are considered for digitization in 
accordance with the Mission guidelines, subject to physical verification, institutional readiness and 
availability of resources. The digitization of eligible manuscript collections is a continuous process, 
executed after execution of the prescribed agreements, creation of metadata, quality assessment and 
compliance with the operational guidelines of GBM.  
 
(b) An allocation of Rs.60 crore has been made for the current financial year under GBM, out of which 
Rs.4.48 crore has already been utilized so far. The Mission provides project-based financial assistance to 
institutions holding manuscript collections to undertake activities relating to the identification, 
documentation, conservation, digitisation and publication of manuscript-based research works. It also 
supports capacity-building programmes for developing expertise in manuscriptology, conservation and 
digitisation. Financial assistance is considered on the basis of proposals received from institutions and 
their appraisal as per the prescribed procedures and guidelines of GBM. 
 

(c) Gyan Bharatam envisages the identification, documentation, conservation, digitisation, research, 
publication and dissemination of India's manuscript heritage irrespective of script, language, dialect, 
tradition, community or geographical location.  
Conservation interventions are undertaken based on the physical condition and specific requirements of 
manuscripts. The Mission also facilitates need-based capacity-building programmes to develop expertise 
among manuscript custodians and other stakeholders in areas such as manuscriptology, conservation and 
digitisation.  
The concerned State Governments and Union Territory Administrations have also been engaged to 
facilitate coordinated efforts and ensure comprehensive coverage of manuscript heritage across the 
country. 
 
(d) Technical assistance and institutional support are facilitated through the designated technology 
partners onboarded for various functions including metadata creation and its integration on National 
Digital Repository (NDR), deployment of equipments, AI-integrated digital platform and long-term data 
storage etc. Proposals received from eligible institutions are considered on case-to-case basis and in 
accordance with the applicable framework, operational requirements, availability of funds etc. and 
implementation is undertaken thereafter in a phased manner as per agreed terms and conditions.

1245.   Shri Saptagiri Sankar Ulaka: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware of reports regarding errors, factual inaccuracies and other 
mistakes in textbooks prescribed and distributed to students of Government schools in Odisha 
and if so, the details thereof, including the classes, subjects and textbooks affected; 
(b)  whether the Government has sought any report or clarification from the Government of Odisha 
regarding such errors and their impact on students and if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether the Government ha s examined if prescribed procedures for academic review, expert 
verification, proofreading and quality checks were followed before printing and distribution of 
such textbooks and if so, the findings thereof; and 
(d)  the steps taken/proposed to be taken by  the Government in coordination with the State 
Government to rectify or replace erroneous textbooks, fix responsibility for lapses and strengthen 
review and quality -control mechanisms to ensure that students receive accurate and error -free 
learning materials? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
 
(a) to  (d):  Education is in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and majority of the schools 
come under the purview of the respective State and UT Government.  The textbook development and 
distribution to students, comes under the domain of State/ UT Government. As informed by the State 
Government of Odisha, National Education Policy, 2020 has been implemented by the Govt. of

1246. THIRU D M KATHIR ANAND: 
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the status of eco-tourism initiatives supported by the Government in 
Tamil Nadu, including the Baralikadu eco -tourism project in the 
Karamadai Forest Range of Coimbatore district within the Nilgiri  
Biosphere landscape, where nature -based tourism activities are 
undertaken with participation of tribal communities; 
(b) the details of the initiatives implemented/proposed to be 
implemented for promoting eco -tourism models that combine 
conservation of forests, rivers and biodiversity with sustainable 
livelihood opportunities for tribal and forest-dwelling communities; 
(c) the details of the programmes undertaken for strengthening visitor 
facilities, interpretation centres, skill development, community 
participation and promotion of eco-tourism destinations across Tamil 
Nadu; 
(d) the details of funds allocated, released and utilised under eco -
tourism, sustainable tourism and community-based tourism schemes 
during the period from 2020-21 to 2025-26; and 
(e) the details of outcomes achieved in terms of tourist arrivals, local 
employment generation, conservation awareness and economic 
benefits to communities residing near protected and forest areas? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM           (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (e):  Development of tourist destinations and products including eco-
tourism is primarily undertaken by the respective State Government/Union 
Territory (UT) Administration. The Ministry complements the efforts of 
States/UTs through various schemes and initiatives. 
 

The Ministry of Tourism through its central sector schemes of 
‘Swadesh Darshan, ‘Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual, Heritage 
Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD) and ‘Assistance to Central Agencies for 
Tourism Infrastructure Development  ’extends financial assistance to the 
State Governments / UT Administrations for tourism infrastructure 
development in the country.  The central financial assistance is being 
extended according to guidelines and based on proposals / detailed project 
reports received from the States and UT Governments.  
 
The guidelines for ‘Challenge Based Destination Development’ has 
been formulated as a sub scheme of Swadesh Darshan 2.0 Scheme to 
enhance tourist experience and to transform tourist destinations as 
sustainable & responsible destinations. 
 
Under the above schemes, the Ministry considers sanctioning a range 
of components which may enhance tourism facilitation at the destinations, 
as per project requirement including those related to tourism core 
products, tourism activities, safety, sanitation, last mile connectivity,  
parking, general site development, soft interventions etc. 
 
The details of projects sanctioned in the State of Tamil Nadu are 
given at Annexure. 
 
With the aim to promote tourism in tribal areas, the Ministry of 
Tourism has issued guidelines along with template for formulation of 
proposal by State Governments and UT Administrations for 'Development 
of Homestays in Tribal Areas' (A sub-scheme of Swadesh Darshan Scheme) 
under Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya  Unnat Gram Abhiyan (PM -JUGA). The 
objective of the initiative is to develop homestays in tribal areas to promote 
responsible tourism and enhance livelihood opportunities for tribal 
communities. The guidelines also focus on technical upskilling and training 
of the Homestay owners. The said initiative includes development of 1000 
homestays with support of Up to ₹5 lakh for village community 
requirement, Up to ₹5 lakh for construction of two new rooms for each 
household and Up  to ₹3 lakh for renovation of existing rooms for each 
household. 
 
Various schemes, programs, and initiatives of the Ministry including 
Paryatan Mitra/Paryatan Didi, Hunar Se Rozgar Tak etc. have been actively 
addressing issues related to skill development, creation of awareness on 
economic benefits, sustainability etc. 
 

In order to provide impetus for development of eco -tourism in the 
country, Ministry of Tourism formulated National Strategies for eco -
tourism and Sustainable Tourism and initiated Travel for LiFE programme 
to promote sustainable tourism in the country and to encourage the 
tourists and tourism businesses to adopt sustainable tourism practices.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1248 
ANSWERED ON 27/07/2026 
 
PROMOTION OF GLOBAL TOURISM AND CULTURAL INFRASTRUCTURE IN 
UTTAR PRADESH 
 
✝1248.SHRI TANUJ PUNIA: 
 
Will the Minister of Culture be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of the schemes currently being implemented by the Government to promote global 
tourism and strengthen cultural infrastructure in the major cultural and religious centres of Uttar 
Pradesh, such as Varanasi, Ayodhya, Mathura and Prayagraj; 
 
(b)whether the Government is considering any special package for the preservation of the 
endangered folkart forms of Uttar Pradesh, such as Nautanki, Charkula dance and 'Kajri Gayan' 
and for providing financial assistance to local artists;  
 
(c)whether if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d)the details of the funds allocated and released to Uttar Pradesh for the said purpose during the 
last two years? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM  
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (c)     Government of India promotes global tourism and strengthen cultural infrastructure 
in India including the major cultural and religious centres of Uttar Pradesh. The Ministry of 
Tourism provides Central Financial Assistance (CFA) to State Governments (including Uttar 
Pradesh) and Union Territory Administrations under Domestic Promotion and Publicity 
including Hospitality Scheme for organizing fairs, festivals, and tourism-related events.  
 
         Ministry of Culture promotes global tourism and strengthen cultural infrastructure in Uttar 
Pradesh through the different Schemes run by this Ministry and its Cultural Institutions. Under 

the Global Engagement Scheme, the Ministry has empanelled Artists/Groups under various art 
forms for performing in the Festival of India (FoIs) abroad. Currently, 627 Artists/Groups are 
empanelled with the Ministry. Out of which, 31 artists/groups are from Uttar Pradesh. 
 
          North Central Zone Cultural Centre with its registered office at Prayagraj provide facilities 
for creative development of arts and literature with special emphasis on folk and tribal arts in its 
Zone including the Uttar Pradesh.  Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) has a 
regional centre at Varanasi which undertakes activities relating to the research, documentation, 
preservation and dissemination of India’s art and Culture heritage including the folk-art forms of 
Uttar Pradesh. National School of Drama supports the promotion and preservation of traditional 
and folk theatre forms, including those from Uttar Pradesh, through its training programmes, 
seminars, workshops, theatre productions and festivals, as part of its regular activities. Similarly, 
the Centre for Cultural Resources and Trailing (CCRT), implement various programmes to 
promote and preserve India’s cultural heritage that supports cultural tourism across the country 
including the Uttar Pradesh.  
           In addition, the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), an organization under the 
Ministry of External Affairs, provides performance opportunities to artists representing diverse 
traditional and folk-art forms of Uttar Pradesh through its monthly cultural programmes 
organized by Zonal Office in Lucknow across the state.  
          ICCR has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with State Government of Uttar 
Pradesh to promote their art and culture abroad.  ICCR sponsors India’s folk-art troupes 
including from the Uttar Pradesh to perform in different countries across the world and also 
sponsors participation of foreign cultural troupes/artists across the country including the Uttar 
Pradesh. During the last two years, ICCR has facilitated participation of over 200 international 
artists in several iconic cultural festivals/events hosted by the State Government of Uttar 
Pradesh.  
 
(d) No funds allocated and released specifically to Uttar Pradesh for the said purpose during 
the last two years.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1249 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
  
e-Waste Management 
 
1249. DR. SAMBIT PATRA: 
  
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has launched any scheme for the management, disposal, and recycling 
of electronic waste (e-waste) and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the number of cases of violation of the national e-waste policy that have come to light during the 
last three years along with the action taken in such cases, State/UT-wise; 
(c) the number of surprise inspections conducted by the Government to ensure compliance with the 
said policy during the last three years along with the action taken against the violators, State/UT-
wise; 
(d) whether cases of dumping of e-waste imported from foreign countries have also come to the notice 
of the Government and if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the details of the policy formulated for the prevention of dumping of e-waste imported from 
foreign countries? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE 
CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (c)  Ministry has notified the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 in November, 2022 under 
the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 after comprehensive revision of the E-Waste (Management) 
Rules, 2016, and the same is in force since 1st April, 2023. These rules provide for managing e-waste 
in an environmentally sound manner and putting in place an improved Extended Producer 
Responsibility (EPR) regime for e-waste recycling wherein all the manufacturer, producer, 
refurbisher and recycler are required to register on portal developed by the Central Pollution Control 
Board (CPCB). These rules promote Circular Economy through EPR regime and scientific 
recycling/disposal of the e-waste.  
 
Under Rule 24 of the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, there is provision for verification and 
audit by the CPCB or through a designated agency, to verify compliance of these Rules through 
random inspection and periodic audit, as deemed appropriate, so as to take action against violations 
of these Rules. CPCB has developed an audit module in the E-Waste EPR portal for carrying out 
audit through mobile app and web application. CPCB has developed guidelines for levying 
Environmental Compensation (EC) under the rules and the same is available at E-waste EPR portal.  
CPCB has also issued direction on 03.07.2026 under Section 5 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 
1986, wherein, State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)/ Pollution Control Committees (PCCs) have 
been directed to carry out audits of recyclers in phased manner. Further, under Schedule-V of the E-
Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, SPCBs/ PCCs have been given the responsibility to monitor 
compliance of EPR and conduct random inspection of recycler and refurbisher and monitoring 

recycling capacity utilization. Information on such violations is maintained by the respective 
SPCBs/PCCs.  
 
(d) & (e) The import and export of hazardous and other wastes is regulated under the Hazardous 
and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) (HOWM) Rules, 2016 notified by 
the Ministry, which provide a comprehensive framework for the transboundary movement of 
hazardous and other wastes in line with the provisions of the Basel Convention. The Rules 
categorically prohibit the import of hazardous and other wastes for the purpose of disposal in India. 
Further, e-waste falling under Basel No. A1180 (waste electrical and electronic assemblies or scrap) 
is listed in Schedule VI of HOWM Rules, 2016, and import of such e-waste is prohibited.
